Before starting this review, I have to say the following: This game is an incredible game, but not an incredible roguelike. For people who are more familiar with other games in this genre, it falls very short of what good roguelike design should be, instead trading mechanical depth and knowledge away for a mass market appeal to gamers who would not normally gel with that style of gameplay. I do not hate the game, but I believe no one has actually voiced the criticism that needs to be stated to the consumer, especially people who see the Roguelike tag and expect a certain level of depth that isn't present. In most roguelites that have come before it, there is very little story or narrative. This is all done for the sake of gameplay, as they were more limited productions that had to choose what to focus on, and a narrative isn't really something that keeps people coming back to a game that can be played infinitely. Supergiant, however, took a gamble and expanded an endless dungeon crawler into a story game that unraveled over many runs, something that no other predecessor had done to completion. When the game was released, the number of people who would not stop gushing about this game came out of the walls just to tell you to play it. A sudden conclusion dawned on me, however, as soon as I started; these people who would not shut up about how great the game is don't know anything about roguelikes; this was their first introduction to the genre, and boy was it far out there in terms of design. A wave of success lauded over this game attracted people who were familiar with the genre, and they were met with an experience that is far removed from what they know a roguelike to be. This is when I discovered the first major issue with the gameplay: hack and slash. This style of combat breaks me open; it's tacky and feels unpolished. There is little depth to actual combat inputs without boons. I could understand choosing a hack-and-slash that had some very fast gameplay, but this was slower and more commitment-based, no dashing to interrupt your attacks, no quick reactions to block or parry; it feels very safe from a design perspective for a mass market appeal. The player can become fully capable of clearing the game within a couple of hours, and there aren't any systems to the gameplay that build on top of each other. The only difficulty of the game comes from learning the one set of attacks and characteristics of the enemies, which, after a couple of runs, you will have completely figured out. So the gameplay runs stale after a couple of hours, so what? Well, the game is meant to be replayed as many times as you want, so if it is falling on its face after a couple of runs, it's lacking in depth, not only of combat but also exploration. Dungeon crawlers are built on exploration, but with the art at hand in the creation of this game, it's not infinitely scalable; there are limited rooms and enemy placements. This goes back to narrative; the game is a story first and a dungeon crawler second. The entire gameplay loop consists of clearing a room and then choosing between a couple of doors, and the reward you get for completing them. This system of picking one door out of multiple is very boring and lacking in player agency. After numerous runs, you'll see every room in the game and know roughly where all the enemies spawn. The preview of rewards is also a poor decision. I understand why it was done since there is no backtracking, and you want to let the player choose what they get. However, being a rogue-LITE, there is meta progression mixed into rewards, so part of the gameplay is choosing whether you can sack your current run to work towards permanently upgrading your character, creating this inverse feedback where to finish the game faster, the player is incentivised to lose, then upgrade their runs to win their runs later. The game fights itself; you don't need to max your upgrades to win once, but it makes it easier. Unlocking the only player agency you can use in the entire game takes a ton of meta currency, making the player progression towards max an awful experience. The dice are the only retort the player can use when they run into a wall of garbage upgrades to choose from. Speaking of choosing, "Alright Timmy, there are 3 doors you can choose from, one has a million dollars, one has a vat of acid, and one has a minigun behind it. After opening a door, you will have to use whatever you pick to kill a gorilla. Good luck!" Arbitrary choices, especially with a limited ability to use player agency to modify those decisions, are what kill a majority of roguelikes. Of the upgrade options presented, a majority are niche or dependent on other abilities. Some of the strongest, however (looking at you Poseidon/Athena dash), don't even need synergy to work very well. It feels like a very mixed bag, where again, you don't really get to spec into exactly what you want, but at the same time, you are mostly dependent on RNG to get a good run. Yes, I hear you Hades fans, no 3 dice rolls are not enough player agency to be anything more than a caddle getting prodded to walk an increasingly narrow strip of road and getting to choose the background scenery as you walk to the slaughterhouse. When the player cannot make decisions that greatly affect how the game operates or gives you rewards besides picking what reward you get when you get one, that game is lacking player agency. I can pick on a million games for doing this exact same thing; however, Hades is where this idea of "Oh weeee, you get a cool upgrade, here's 3 random abilities that I pulled out of my blazing ass that have a loose mechanical or thematic tie together to fire" comes from. This is the game that popularized the concept to a mainstream audience. The amount of praise this game gets for having such a low skill ceiling without the difficulty modifiers, practically no player agency, and not expanding on its combat system at all after the tutorial is bewildering to me as someone who loves to play practically every major roguelike that has ever come out. To a mainstream gamer, this was a very accessible game, but to anyone familiar with the genre, this is very disappointing. Roguelikes are mainly determined to present a player with a required set of skills the player themselves must develop to reach and finish the end, afterwards they get access to harder content and can continue to pursue it, if they wish. Hades, however, is wearing the skin of a roguelike when in reality it's a story game. Its micro and macro (room combat & upgrade decisions) gameplay is uninspired for a roguelike. After the story is complete and most players have finished their first run, they stop. The reason is that the narrative is the only reason they were interested in the game; the gameplay can't stand on its own. I have experienced this myself, as well as looking through my friends' list, and I can see it plain as day. Of my 6 friends who own this game, 5 of them killed the final boss once, saw the basic ending, and left. There was nothing here for them anymore; the narrative was what allowed them to power through the slog of gameplay, and upon removing that, there is no incentive to play the game anymore. That's not to discredit the narrative, because it is by far the strongest selling point of the game, but when people say that Hades is one of the best games of all time, I really wonder if they have played it more than once. I highly doubt those rose-tinted glasses won't crack before the end of a second playthrough, after a player already knows what to do, nothing is new anymore, and there is no new narrative to pull them through. Realistically, A rougelike should be just as enjoyable the second time you play through it, since it should be able to stand the test of time, but I feel this game can't. It's an excellent one-off game with beautiful visuals, story, voice acting, and writing, and also a mediocre roguelike.

Will maybe write an in-depth review once I beat it, but the tl;dr It's a roguelike that does everything right in terms of the genre. While it can get a bit repetitive as all roguelikes tend to do, it tries to break this up by giving the chance to include optional difficulty modifiers on your subsequent runs. Every run feels like a step in the right direction, providing resources to buff your future delves into hell. It's high octane, fast + flashy movements with a supporting soundtrack that is phenomenal. I highly recommend this as a game to play 1-2 times a week and just slowly make your way to the end. Or rush it, if you feel like it, but you might tire on it to quick if you do.

Hades is addictive, and I say this as a former alcoholic. The gameplay loop begs me to play one more run, just one more. I want to see what abilities I'll get, try a new weapon, try a new version of the weapon, unlock the story, etc. It's so incredibly satisfying and polished. Before Hades I had played no Supergiant games, but I have gone back and played some Pyre, as well as Bastion, and it's incredible to see the progression that they achieved. It seems like those games were hinting at a grander experience that culminated in Hades. I don't know if this is a forever game for me, but I've got over 100 hours between this save and the one on my Switch. I also have 150+ hours in Hades II. Neither have gotten stale yet, and there are mods that I haven't explored yet. I bought this twice, both on sale and I feel as if I ripped off Supergiant.

Hades is one of the most replayable games I’ve ever played. Every run feels different thanks to the shifting Boons, weapon aspects, and room layouts, and even after countless attempts, the game still finds ways to surprise you. The reason to keep coming back to Hades isn't just the thrills you'll get battling through hell, but the characters and stories you learn about along the way. The game rewards persistence not only with better skills and builds, but with new dialogue, evolving relationships, and deeper lore that unfolds run after run. The combat is fast, smooth, and incredibly satisfying, but what really elevates the experience is how alive the world feels—even in the underworld. It’s rare for a roguelike to make you care about the entire cast, but Hades absolutely nails it. If you love tight gameplay, meaningful progression, and a narrative that grows the more you play, Hades is easily a must-buy. Just one more run? Always. When will i beat this game? Soon.

Every escape attempt writes a new chapter in the Underworld Prince’s ever-growing saga!

This is my first time playing rouge-lite/rouge-like game, and so far I am loving it! This game is designed in a way that you need to die multiple times to know the lore better but that doesn't mean you have too die (though you will for sure many times ! xd )You play as Zagreus who is attempting to escape the underworld which is ever-shifting (procedurally generated) by defying his father. On this journey of yours, the Olympian gods will assist you for you attempt of escaping the underworld. Each time you die you get to manually interact with the characters in the house of hades, which helps you understand the lore and characters in depth and also the characters will react to your death (like the way you died or by whom you got destroyed ), This game is very fast paced, hack and slash style, dungeon crawler rouge-lite with polished, no software bugs or glitches experience ( but there are bugs in-game though pun intended ). You will have an absolute blast playing this game, 101% recommended ! Also you will get the Music Kit "Darren Korb, Hades" in Counter-Strike 2 after you have completed 5 Hrs of playtime of this game so be sure to use it and speaking of music, the soundtrack of this game is an absolute masterpiece of art. Especially the main menu theme of this game is one of, not thee best among the games I have played ! So go for it and attempt the escape from ever-shifting underworld

⭐ 10/10 – Hades ruined my sleep schedule and I’m thanking it. I bought Hades thinking, “I’ll do a couple runs before bed.” Three days later I’m still dodging imaginary projectiles in my kitchen and calling my daughter Zagreus by accident. Every time I die, the game pats me on the head and says, “Good try, buddy, now go talk to your gods again like it’s a Greek family reunion.” And somehow… I LIKE IT. Combat? Smooth like butter melting on a lava rock. Story? I went from “I don’t care about Greek mythology” to “I would die (again) for Megaera.” Music? I swear the soundtrack added +5 to my real-life cardio. Hades is the only game where losing feels like winning, winning feels like cheating, and cheating feels like destiny. If dopamine had a physical form, it would look exactly like a gold Daedalus hammer. TL;DR: I escaped the Underworld but not the addiction. Send help. Actually no, don’t send help—send more runs. 10/10 Would get stabbed by a butterfly ball again.

OK... I have MANY things to say... mainly in the pros and cons of this game... don't worry this is NOT a jab at the game but holy literal hell this game is a doozy... onto the pros and cons... going to take a LONG break before I play Hades 2 thats for sure... Pro 1: Replayability... seriously its BUILT into the game... every time you die, you come back with various items from your trips through the location of Hades, mainly Tartarus, Asphodel, Elysium, and finally the Entrance to Hades... mainly you have to get by a LOT or if your lucky, VERY LITTLE to get to the surface... I'm no speed runner but managed to beat the game once near the 20 minute mark, pretty sure speed runners are laughing at that time since they normally would just zip by things... Con 1: The List of Fated Prophecies - mainly this isn't a con persay... it has a LOT of goodies so you SHOULD be going for them but the main issue... THERE IS NO QUEST TRACKER IN THE GAME... mainly when on a run if your trying to go for a specific fated prophecy you HAVE to remember them after looking at Zagreus's desk... Pro 2: Side Quests - Mainly you HAVE to save a LOT of Nectar and Ambrosia... especially for the Epilogue but that's for its own kind of thing later... for now you have Nectar to save for to gain hearts with MANY NPC's... again its own kind of list after this... Con 2: Conditions for main story end and epilogue - now I'm not knocking the Epilogue but... *BREATHS IN* This games epilogue Epilogue is good in many ways but HORRIBLE in others... first off you HAVE to beat the main game 10 FREAKING times!... if your having fun you will enjoy this... THAT is the easy part since all you have to do is kick Hade's ass!... the God not the location... but thats not the main con of this... no... the main con is simply this... you NEED A TON OF NECTAR and AMBROSIA to gain full trust fo 6 of the 8 Olympian gods for the Epilogue ending after unlocking their 7th heart since those are locked until specific conditions are passed... I'll save you time by explaining each... Zeus - Mainly talk to ALL Gods until they give their opinions on Zeus, after that, wait till Zeus says something on reconnecting with Hades and Hades response after... after that, 6 Nectar and 1 Ambrosia Poseidon - Simple... fish... fish in the Underworld like you never fished before... when you think you fished enough... fish some more... I'm not kidding... have Fish in your inventory after 18 fishes are acquired and have at least ONE on your person to unlock the 7th slot... after that you talk to Poseidon and again... 6 Nectar and 1 Ambrosia... you can sell your fish to the chef in the House of hades afterwards so profit! Athena - Mainly exhaust her dialogue on her complimenting your strength, should unlock after awhile and when you do... 6 Nectar and 1 ambrosia... Ares - Mainly slay 10,000 enemies and make sure to give 6 Nectar and 1 ambrosia, its in the list of Fated prophecies but when I got it, already passed that mark by a mile... mainly should happen automatically more or less if you have the blood vial in your inventory as well... honestly bit hard for me to remember after who knows how many runs. Artemis - Mainly exaust Artemis's dialogue on her talking about her partner, Callisto, once you do, automatically unlocks the 7th slot, 6 nectar and 1 ambrosia. Hermes - A surprising 8 hearts, Hermes's requires 6 Nectar and 2 Ambrosia but you NEED to max out his Keepsake the Lambent Plume, you don't need it to have any bonuses on it, just max it out to three stars for the 8th heart unlock and what not... little surprised by that... Dionysus - Simply put... BE a party animal... max out the bonds of at least 6 different people, give 6 nectar and 1 Ambrosia to the Drinking God himself to more or less get on his good side... should be one of the latter gods you befriend... he has insane Boons that mix well with others so use him A LOT... guy is your best friend here. Aphrodite - Mainly max out your bonds with three spacific NPC's, Dusa, Thanatos, and Megaera or Meg for short and trigger three different dialogs with the Goddess... you'll need 6 Nectar and 1 ambrosia for Aphrodite after as well... Demeter - Surprisingly the easiest to complete for the Epilogue ending after you unlock her after your first ending run (by that I mean you have to beat the game ONCE for her to appear), just give 6 Nectar, after that well if you play the game more, one Ambrosia... Enough said people you have your list... its up to you on how to save up ALL that Nectar and Ambrosia but know that its a grind in hell itself... To make a meme of sorts and from a youtube channel's video... here is something perfect for this game: Sisyphus!... I understand! The definition of Insanity is doing the exact same thing over and over again... expecting different results... THIS game is the literal personification of bashing your head against a brick wall and sooner or later your head breaks or the wall will... in this case... the wall broke... after 50+ runs against it... you CAN break the wall with enough effort... but you will be put through literal hell in doing so... I both love and loathe this game and I recommend it for all who enjoy the Greek Mythos with subtle changes here and there and boy oh boy if you like Rogue-likes... I love it but damn I'm burned out... until I play Hades 2 and stuff not playing a game like this for a bit... again I believe my hours and time was well worth the price but damn was I put through hell in a literal and metaphorical sense... for now I must rest... but while this review may not be seen... I hope it helps a small few because damn!... some conditions for some NPC's be insane...

Hades is a perfect example of what video games should provide for gamers. Amazing fast gameplay, amazing boss fights, amazing quests, amazing details, amazing progressing story and different variants of character builds every run. Nonstop entertaining. Even though each run has same mobs and same bosses, each run is unique because different character builds, weapons, weapon aspects and keepsakes completely changes the gameplay. Prevents you from getting bored if you don't do the same build each run. Game has really good character designs. I loved all of characters. They are well written. You can also romance some characters. It is a perfect story about the rebel son of hades. Hades has a perfect satisfying ending and it has a perfect true ending that ended the plot without any questions in my head. Zagreus is a perfect protagonist we all loved him easily and we watched him achieving his dreams and reuniting his family. He didn't give up and fought until the very end. Great characters, gods, goddesses and heroes from Greek mythology. I really like Greek mythology. I am really grateful from Supergiant Games for making this absolute masterpiece for gaming industry and for gamers. HADES IS BEST ROGUE-LITE IN MY OPINION. And best indie game of 2020. Hades has 93 Metacritic on PC and it totally deserves it. Too many people doesn't know this but Hades is rogue-lite, not rogue-like. It has meta progress. After I heard about Hades 2 finally coming out of early access, I thought I'd give Hades another shot. When the game came out on Switch, I bought it - then promptly got stuck due to the limitations of the Joycons. Got it on a nice sale, and got to say that after 150 hours, it's an excellent use of that time. Beating the game took a long time, but after I beat the final boss the first time, that's when the real game starts. I probably did around 50-60 clears to get all of the achievements, but I could have probably done it faster if I tried to optimize. However, why would I try to optimize? This game is super fun to play with all of the different permutations from boons, weapons, and pact of punishment modifiers. I'd be able to make a lot of my own goals for getting through a run, and even did some light speed-running (18 minutes or so is speed-running for me :D). Art style? Great. Music? Maybe unbeaten in terms of the variety of music that is available. Seriously, some of the singing was weirdly good from Orpheus. Themes and storyline about family and rekindling relationships? More wholesome than I realized it was going to be. Theseus being annoying and Zagreus picking up on it and roasting him? Funny. Many of the creative aspects of this game should be a standard for what games can do with early access feedback: have a strong core idea, then refine and polish for as long as humanly possible. You can really tell Supergiant took their time with this, and that's why it won a bazillion awards. There are some things that I think could have been explained a bit better to the player. Some of the conversations and side-quests seem to happen in a random order, but to get all of the achievements I had to max out conversations with certain characters. Thanatos, for example, just stopped appearing until another quest was completed, but I was trying to max rank his relationship for his companion buddy. Also, wish that the weapons were easier to unlock and use earlier on - I finally got some of the sweetest aspects towards the end of the game when I no longer needed them. Overall, very important game to set the standard of work that can go into polishing a release - and also just a very fun top-down roguelike that teaches you to stick with it and eventually you can get that same Souls-like gratification out of it.

With Hades II getting so much praise, I finally decided to check out the original Hades—and with my new Steam Deck, this felt like the perfect time to jump in. Now I get why everyone calls this one of the best Deck games out there. The game looks and runs great on both my Deck and PC. The visuals are simple but stylish, with vibrant colors and a unique art direction that instantly stands out. It’s always pleasant to look at, even during the chaos. The story won’t rival The Witcher or Game of Thrones, but it doesn’t have to. The writing is sharp, the characters are memorable, the voice acting is fantastic, and every interaction adds flavor to the experience. It’s packed with style and personality. Gameplay is where Hades really shines. It’s fast, smooth, and incredibly addicting. The moment you fail a run, you’re already itching to jump back in. Even with the repetitive loop, it never feels stale thanks to the huge variety of boons, weapons, and upgrades that change how each escape attempt plays. I’ve been playing it during downtime at work, and it’s become part of my regular rotation of indies and roguelikes. Whether you’re traveling, waiting around, or just relaxing on the couch, Hades is perfect for quick sessions or longer runs. You’ll die a lot, but it never feels frustrating—unlike Souls games, this one doesn’t make me want to throw a controller. There’s something almost meditative about a clean 10–15 minute run. No, it’s not a giant cinematic AAA epic, but it’s not trying to be. It’s a stylish, fun, endlessly replayable action game that nails exactly what it sets out to do. Highly recommended—especially on the Steam Deck. 9/10.

[h1]"Few tales are told of Hades, whose very name inspires fear and penitence, reminding us of the inevitable fate which we all share."[/h1] [h1]Introduction[/h1] [b]This review is based on playing on the Steam deck.[/b] I've never been particularly good at roguelike or lite games, but having heard repeatedly that Hades is such an interesting and fun experience pulled me towards giving it a shot at long last. But was it able to survive a full run, or did it die on the shores of Tartarus? [table] [tr] [th][b]🟩 Positives[/b][/th] [th][b]🟥 Negatives[/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]🟩 Fun, fast-paced gameplay that requires learning and strategy to master. 🟩 Hundreds, if not thousands, of possible combinations of skills and abilities to blend in your journey for discovery. 🟩 A soundtrack that absolutely shouldn't have hit as hard as it did. 🟩 A unique art style that doesn't diminish the game but gives it noticeable character and personality that is often hard to capture in games.[/td] [td]🟥 Runs do become boring after a while, with only the odd thing changing or a bit of storyline across what can be a 45-minute to an-hour run. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [table] [tr][th]🏆Achievements[/th][/tr] [td] A somewhat tricky completion as not many of the achievements are straightforward. I recommend using a guide to complete some of the more vague ones to save yourself some time.[/td] [/table] [h1]Story[/h1] Hades takes place in the Underworld as you control Zagreus, the son of none other than Hades himself, who has sought to escape his father's realm and seek his fortune on the surface. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3614351173 With the assistance of your mother, Nyx, Zagreus has gained the attention of Olympus, and the Gods there are offering their aid to his plight as well. With countless foes ahead and the aid of the Gods, Zagreus must fight through the layers of the Underworld and seek his freedom at any cost. But what awaits him at the end of his journey? [h1]Gameplay Analysis[/h1] [h3]Traversing the hells.[/h3] As with most action roguelike games, fast, frenetic gameplay and quick decision-making are what help define Hades. Movement is fluid and simplistic but requires a level of experience to master. Traversing the landscapes can be treacherous at times, so understanding the controls is crucial. Hades is fairly straightforward mechanically. You will face off against waves of enemies within each room and then are given a choice of two following rooms to enter, with their specific rewards for completion. At the end of each floor, you are presented with a boss fight that is static for each level of the Underworld, and after this fight, you can ascend to the next level. Dying means you have to start again from the beginning of the run. [h3]Weapons fit for a God.[/h3] In addition to the colossal amount of abilities and skills, you can unlock and discover across your playthrough. You will also get to choose from a selection of weapons that drastically change the way you play. The starting sword you have is a good all-rounder, but each weapon you unlock will have strengths and weaknesses you will have to discover and overcome to survive. [h3]Power on speed dial.[/h3] The part that makes Hades unique is the God's power mechanics, each of the Olympian Gods can give you a fraction of their power to use, across a selection of skills, randomised each time to three choices. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3614351557 Each of the Gods has a specific thing they can provide, such as Ares has a lot of offensive abilities, while Hermes can improve speed and dodging. Blending these with your choice of weapon and playstyle can be a lot of fun, especially experimenting with what works and what doesn't. [h1]Audio and Visual[/h1] Not the most impressive visual experience on the market, but one of the most unique. The art style is chocked full of character, detail and expression that you immediately feel pulled into the story purely based on a visual sense. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3614352429 The audio is much the same, not particularly redefining anything, but is loaded with its style and personality that it's hard to not feel connected with it. In cooperation with the visual style, these aspects work extremely well together. [h1]Steam Deck Performance and Specifications[/h1] Hades performs extremely well on the Steam Deck, and I'd probably go as far as to say that this is a staple for the hardware. At full charge, you'd get two to three hours of gameplay out of it, which is decent considering the style of the game. [h1]Final Thoughts - Excellent[/h1] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2529084785]Review chart here.[/url] Hades is a phenomenal game that plays extremely well and consistently provides a fun, fast and frenetic gameplay experience that is loaded with character and story. Aiming for 100% completion does weigh the game down considerably, but the general experience with the game was nothing but high. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of good stories, roguelites or unique art styles. [quote]Ransacking the Underworld can become extremely tiresome, so head on over to, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/43064204/] Hell, Purgatory and Paradise[/url] to get the peace you long for.[/quote]

Let me be honest right off the bat: I absolutely HATE woke ish, no matter where. Series, movies, and especially games? Doesn't matter. Eff off with it. Leave me the frak alone with that propaganda noise, because that's all it is. Noise. Insufferable, obnoxious noise. I have absolutely nothing against gay people, I'm 100% against the whole agenda being pushed by deranged lunatics. Now, having said that, is there stuff in Hades I could have lived without? Sure, there is a scene and a line or two that made me roll my eyes, and I'm not going to spoil any of it. If you know about the game, you most likely have heard about the noise as well, especially over the sequel. However... None of this changes the fact that Supergiant delivered an absolute masterpiece of a game. I'm 49, I've played thousands of games, but only very few have had such an emotional impact on me. They don't pull any punches, they hit you straight in the gut, stomp on your heart, rip out your soul, and you keep coming back for more, because it's so damn brilliant. I've cried during some dialogue parts, that's how heavy they hit, and I'm not ashamed to admit it. Is the game hard? Yes, it is. It took me over 80 attempts to get my first victory. Why didn't I give up? Because first of all, I'm not a gawddarn quitter, and second because every loss still gave me something back. A new discussion with a side character. A new lore drop. More Darkness to upgrade my Mirror and finally get that one key skill unlocked that made a difference. With each defeat, I learned, I adapted, I changed my style. I got knocked down, shrugged, and went in for another round, and by attempt #124 I officially "beat" the game, or at least the main story. Greg Kasavin, the main writer behind Hades' story, is just brilliant. Sure, he had a whole mythology to base his work on, but still. The way the story gets pushed forward gently, in small steps, and still ends up hitting you like a truck at times is nothing short of amazing. Getting that first victory, and then facing what comes next? Holy crap, I'm still shivering over the impact it had on me, that's how good/awful it was. Yes, the duality of it is truly mind-boggling. The combat itself is infuriating at first, then becomes second-nature. What first was a seemingly impossible barrier to overcome soon turns into a breeze, runs end up getting shorter, you no longer worry about how to get there, but just how fast you get there, and with what build. Over the course of the game, your perception will change. Boons you thought were amazing at first will become obsolete or downright useless because you adapted your style, but again, I'm not going to spoil anything. If you haven't played this game yet, do yourself a favor and do so. Don't give up, what awaits you is one of the best games ever made, and I'm not saying that lightly. Getting angry, feeling like rage-quitting because you died again at that one particular boss? That's fine, put the controller down, cool off, get some rest, and then try again. You'll surpass the obstacles, and you're going to love what comes afterwards, promised. Oh, and the soundtrack? Effin fantastic too! Darren Korb and Ashley Lynn Barrett delivered something that you'll want to listen to a lot. In fact, I have the soundtrack on my phone so that I can listen to it while I drive in my Tesla. There's woke ish, and there's "Eh, it's one line in a whole epic, who cares", and Supergiant definitely belongs in the second category. There's no virtue signaling, there's no forced politics, it's all based on the mythology, so you knew what to expect. Nothing more, nothing less. Hades? Absolute masterpiece. Highly recommended by someone with decades of gaming experience.

Let's preface this simply by saying, I enjoyed my first 50 hours with this game. Interesting character dynamics, fun varied combat, challenging but satisfying combat, all around I enjoyed nearly all of that 50 hours; But you wanna know why I have an extra 30 hours? Achievement hunting, specifically ONE Achievement. Now, I'll be the bigger man and won't spoil what it was, but I'll explain a bit about this game's rouge-like element. Each of the games zones are made out of rooms. Combat, challenges, survive etc. There's a particular type of room called Encounter Rooms. They often give great benefits. Issue is, they're also bloody rare. You can go 10-20 runs without seeing one. To get 3 achievements, you need to find each of the 3 zones encounter rooms and that's not all. Some of these achievements can only be done AFTER finishing the prior one so if you low-ball cant get a certain encounter in a previous zone, you're SOOL for a while. Worse part is, you can customize the difficulty of your runs, you can make Zagreus stronger or weaker as you see fit, but all that pales to the sheer fact you cant control Encounter Rooms. It's literal RNG baked into the game. So you really can't cheese this outside letting the mobs kill you after wasting 15 minutes into a run. Overall, Great game but the encounter rooms made it overstay its welcome. Won't immediately try out Hades 2 now its fully released But I hope they did fix this of all things.

[TL;DR: I heavily enjoyed the story, gameplay, and art/sound and would say this game is top tier and definitely worth playing for $25! Honestly, probably my favorite game as of writing this. I beat my first run last night on my 45th attempt.] To start, the story of the game is captivating. I’m someone who cannot give two flying ♥♥♥♥♥ about a game if I don’t have a story or character to get invested in. Hades has an enchantingly immersive story that works seamlessly hand-in-hand with the game progression in a way that literally feels like magic. There are over a dozen named, unique characters with well-written and witty dialogue (especially funny if you’re knowledgeable about Greek mythology) to look forward to interacting with through the game. I usually find myself getting bored in roguelike games but the story in Hades kept me curious and playing for hours. As for the gameplay, I’m more than satisfied. The keybinds are customizable, playing on both M&K and controller feels nice. This game can work for someone of any skill level, with there being options to make the game easier / more story-focused for those who aren’t mechanically skilled or harder for those who want to challenge themselves. I’ve had runs where I just felt like spamming buttons and I had a blast. I’ve had runs where I wanted to play super strategically and also had a blast. I think anyone could enjoy this game if the genre is up their alley. There’s multiple parts of the game to become invested in, obviously there’s the main run / bosses to try and beat, but there’s also a friendship system and several aspects of the game that involve upgrading and purchasing that doesn’t feel super grindy- even when I’m purposely trying to “grind”. There’s a trading system that makes acquiring certain materials very forgiving and an additional note (for those who love it just as much as I do): there’s a fishing mechanic! I also enjoy that there are realistic achievements in the game, which is great if you enjoy challenging yourself to 100% because you’re a lunatic completionist (I both fear and respect you). Now the art/sound aspect of this game is probably my favorite, and it’s worth noting this goes heavily with the story. Every character has a beautiful, original design with a comic-esque artstyle and incredible voice-acting. This, plus the equally beautiful scenery, aided in the seamless and immersive feel of the game. I personally became really attached and involved in the characters, the locations, and learning everything about them. I think the design and takes on all the characters are really unique while staying true to the original mythos. The music in the game is also really fitting and pleasant, so I don’t find myself wanting to turn it off and open up Spotify like I usually do for games. Overall, I highly recommend this game especially if you’re a person who loves stories and loves getting obsessed with a diverse cast of characters!

Hades Review Hades is actually the very first indie title I dove into after getting my Steam Deck, and I’ve been exploring a lot of indie games since—like Hollow Knight, which I gave a solid 9 out of 10. But this review is all about Hades. Hades is a beautifully vibrant game with a stunning art style and a really eye-catching, artistic approach. I’m a huge fan of Greek mythology, so seeing all those mythological characters brought to life is just fantastic. Let’s start with the combat: it’s fast-paced, fluid, and keeps you on your toes at all times. This is exactly the kind of gameplay I love—really dynamic and engaging. The story isn’t mind-blowing, but it’s definitely easy to follow and pretty good for what it is. I’ve put a ton of hours into Hades and I still feel like I haven’t seen all the dialogue or content. I’ve escaped Hades maybe 20 or 30 times now, and even though I’ve seen the credits roll, it doesn’t feel like I’ve truly "finished" everything the game has to offer. I really don’t have many complaints. If I had to nitpick, I’d say it would be nice to have more bosses—there are only four main bosses total, and maybe a DLC or additional content would be great for that. Also, while there are lots of different builds, you can tell that some godly boons—like those from Artemis and Ares—are just a bit better than others. For example, I found Aphrodite’s boons less useful in my playthroughs. Still, it’s an amazing, addictive game and I’m really looking forward to Hades II. I’d definitely give this one a 9.5 out of 10.

More rouge-lite games should take inspiration from Hades's approach to story-telling!

[h1][i]Hades[/i] was my first roguelite, and I couldn’t have picked a better introduction. I was completely hooked; it easily became a favorite.[/h1] [hr][/hr] [h2]Gameplay[/h2] It took around 20 attempts before I managed to complete an escape. The Pact of Punishment is then unlocked, which lets you customize the difficulty. It keeps things fresh and lets you gather materials to upgrade weapon aspects. Each of the six weapons has four different aspects with unique gimmicks, and mixing them with boons and hammer upgrades makes every run feel unique. Each region has its twist: Tartarus as the standard, Asphodel with rivers of magma, Elysium with reviving Exalted, and the Temple of Styx with its Satyr Tunnels. [h2]Progression[/h2] One thing I appreciate is that failing an attempt never feels like a waste. You always take something back with you, resources you can use for different things. Mirror of Night upgrades help you progress easier on your next attempts, unlocking weapons gives you more playstyle options, and you can purchase customizations for the House of Hades. Each run progresses the story through new character dialogues, so even failed attempts feel meaningful. [h2]Presentation[/h2] The game’s visual identity pulled me in; it’s actually one of the reasons I tried it. The character illustrations look stunning, the environments in each region are unique, and the voice work is immersive. The more I played, the more invested I became in the characters and the world; it even made me want to learn more about Greek mythology. By the time I moved on to [i]Hades II[/i], I was already buying books about Greek myths because the game made me curious. [hr][/hr] Overall, [i]Hades[/i] is an incredible experience; I’d especially recommend it to anyone who enjoys Greek mythology. Whether you’re new to roguelites or not, it’s absolutely worth playing.

The game really has a finished and unique feel masterfully driving a player into unirritating grinding and having fun from dying. Good job devs!
the best way i could describe hades is "roguelike for people that don't like roguelikes" - despite this descriptor people who do like roguelikes will still probably like the game a lot

I bought the game on a discount after recently getting into roguelike and roguelite titles, so I figured I’d finally give Hades a chance. My first few runs went terribly, you die fast, you learn nothing, and everything feels brutal. But then you start noticing enemy attack patterns, you get further, you reach the bosses….. and when you die there, you just want to smash your controller. I was completely stuck on the third boss. Nothing was working. I was this close to uninstalling the game and letting it rot somewhere in my massive library. But then it happens, you finally understand how each God works, which boons fit your playstyle, and you put together a build that actually feels good. With that build, I beat the third boss for the first time… and even managed to kill Hades himself!, roughly 20 hours in. And after that? Everything changes. Suddenly the game clicks. It becomes an obsession. You constantly think about your next run, your next build, your next crazy combination. And it just keeps going in the best possible way. 10/10 a masterpiece.

36 hours in and I will likely not add much more (once I get a bit of rest from this game, I'll probably continue with Hades II). It was fun, I beat the final boss like 5 or 6 times (you need 10 to finish the story though). I just can't find a reason to play more hours as there is not much more to explore except the remaining bits of story.

Really enoyable game! It took me some time to make some progress because this is the first rogue-lite i've ever played (and also the first game I played with a controller instead of keyboard and mouse), but I love that the game rewards you for trying again and again and being persistent :) the art and the music are just beautiful and even though I could predict a lot of the story elements bc im a mythology nerd, the characters are beautifully written and the story keeps you interested! and if you dont care about the story (like my roommate does), the mechanics have very high replayability! Excited to try the second game, after i've collected all achievements and prizes that is :)
I started saying "mhh this gameplay is not quite for me" then became addicted quite soon. Honestly a great experience.

As far as rouguelikes go, this game is probably one of the best, if not the flat-out winner. It gives you just enough story progression and power grow so you don't feel too frustrated with the constant deaths. The combat is crisp and satisfying, and the variety of weapons means you can spend runs upon runs perfecting builds. Besides that, the art in this game is absolutely incredible, the character designs are surprisingly original and the story is very engaging. Would recommend 100%!
best game i've played in the genre, has ruined all other "rogue-likes" for me -- and besides being a great game, it's a real work of art 10/10, would get sucked into again

Hades is a fast and fun action game where every run feels exciting. The combat is smooth, the weapons are satisfying to use, and the story keeps growing each time you try to escape the Underworld. The characters are memorable, the visuals look great, and the music fits perfectly. It is easy to pick up, challenging in a good way, and very rewarding to play. Excited to jump into Hades 2 now!
The loop pulls you back in every time it starts to get stale, and before you know it you're careening around the map creating chaos.

I will admit in advanced that I played the sequel prior to this, with the intention of simply gleaning the sense of plot and rush out imminently. As the played time corroborated, I was enthralled, in the most positive way imaginable though by the magnificent ambient of the game. It will only do it unjust to dismiss it as a mere masterpiece of game level design or a roguelike epitome, despite ascribed accurately, since its splendor resides in between the careful organization of the plot with the concise and delicate game play design. That is to say, and please don't be disguised, this game is as good in its game mechanic as in its narrative affinity, but both aspect is merely prosaic when compares to the coalesced ensemble of them. The game itself provides sufficient impetus for the merging in the dialogues while the story guide the advocacy for the runs, it is truly rare to find another game that bears even remotely similar sense of balance to that in this game. It really is a bellwether of what a modern video game should pertained. Thus, for reviews of this game, both focusing on its mechanic and plot would be a remiss, and fall prey to superficially digression. (although the performance and display is beyond perfection and along should be praise worthy for its success) Please play this game, as any aspect of it remains unassailable and inconceivable to you before actually immersing yourself in the underworld and the boundless set backs it entails.

Solid game, fun lore, impressive voice acting, fun mechanics.. just an overall great rogue-like. It has a setting to make it chill out on subsequent play-throughs so the game gets easier with every play-through. Pick it up, any time, I can't see this game ever really aging. It's a fun experience.

A bit repetitive insofar as I would've liked to see more enemy and area variety, but a very solid roguelite gameplay loop. The gradual pace at which you unlock dialogue and develop the story is well-designed.
Love the game design and voice acting. This is my first Roguelike and I'm finally getting the hang of it.

What can I say that 100 other positive reviews haven't already. I'm not a rogue-lite gamer; This game is fantastic. If you love Supergiant's previous titles like Transistor or Bastion then you know what you're in for: top notch writing, gorgeous music that ramps up as you near each checkpoint. Great modernised characterisations of classic Grecian pantheon archetypes. Well worth it at any discount, still worth it at full price.
This is the single BEST game on my library, I love this game, and to believe that It runs on my 2013 mac, is supprising, and it runs at a smooth 60fps
The main character, Zagreus, must escape an underground empire by fighting & befriending the many denizens of the Underworld. Basically the same game as Undertale, so play if you enjoyed that.
Hard enough to make it challenging enough but not hard enough to rage. I like the variety of weapons and settings.
very fun satisfying roguelike. the fact that there is new dialogue every time you die is very well thought of. (21,020 voice lines in total)

The game has been very fun so far. I haven't been able to complete a run yet, but I'm getting closer and closer and it's very exciting. The game can definitely frustrating at times when you're deep into a run and die, but I can never stay away from the game for long. The art is another reason I love this game, it's beautiful!
Simply fantastic ! 100%-ing a game comes rarely, this game more than well is deserving of this. To think the second has even more content, I shudder at the thought
Slash and smash monsters and spirits while you try and escape living in Hell :) Great music to jam to while pretending to escape our own Hellish reality

Fantastic game, Great 2d graphics, good attention to detail on mythological figures, great game to pick up and play on multiple short sessions, I wish the combat felt a little bit less spammy on dodges but still good variety of weapons and boons to choose from that make the game feel fresh.
It's really good. I wish I had a more insightful review than that, but I don't. If you like dungeon crawlers odds are you will enjoy this game.

at the start of the game, you will feel reaaaally slow or weak or all of the above, but the amount of power you get after just a couple runs makes up for all of it lol. this game is really fun and i only have 6 hours in it which WILL increase soon :D there are so many little interactions too, between gods and characters depending on what you do. it doesnt affect the game too much, but it is really fun to experience. definately recommend before you have to go through more of my terrible spelling and such lol

Hades is a fun roguelike experience, where the player feels themselves becoming stronger and stronger after each attempt, leading to a strong sense of accomplishment. While at first slow and extremely challenging by experimenting with the wide variety of different weapons and boons (skills gained randomly in runs) the player will slower become more attuned to the combat within the game. It definitely feels very rewarding when you find a build that you can successfully beat runs with consistently by combining weapons skills and certain boons to make explosive combinations: the variety in this game is unreal as there are hundreds of different abilities to experiment with and combine together, but admittedly most of them are quite useless. My only gripe is that there are some issues when playing this game on deck, mainly some weirdly long loading times, especially when booting up the game. I have no idea why this happens and it my just be an issue I am experiencing.

I die... so much... in this game! But you know what! That's kinda the point and expected! I sometimes wish I died less, but... This is simply a weird, funny, comical, yet great game, and it's difficult to really say why. It's just fun!

Absolute 10/10 game, challenging but rewarding fights, simple and fast gameplay, in-depth upgrade system, amazing ost, peak artstyle, cant say enough good about it. Thank you supergiant games for blessing my neurons with this experience

If you want a fast paces rogue like that keeps you engaged, this is it!! It is very challenging tho, and you might get frustrated having to go all the way back to the beginning when you die, but they give you a variety of weapons and power ups to keep things interesting.

One of the best Rogue-lites on the market: a nearly endless amount of content that doesn't get old, thanks to the excellent gameplay, breathtaking art, fabulous characters, stellar music, and the sheer quality and quantity of the perfectly voice-acted dialogue... not to mention the myriad of different weapons, powers, and other ways to customize your runs. Hades sets a new standard for the genre.

My play time is low on steam as I initially played through Hades on Xbox, then once again on switch. Regardless. Absolute gem of a game, and easily one of my all time favorites. Found my love for the rougelike genre through it. Highly recommend. 10/10

I cannot believe I waited this long to get on the Hades train. Rogue-likes and battle-oriented games are often intimidating to me, but this one is actually very manageable given it's different game modes. Story is so compelling and characters are fantastic, but you don't need to hear that from me.

I'm not generally a rogue-like fan but Hades has so much going on to make it feel fresh each time. The structure/size of the home base area gives you a solid break between runs and leaves you feeling like you need to go out just one more time to unlock the next thing. Very well designed and polished.
One of the best roguelikes ever, with enough difficulty that "god mode" feels like normal difficulty while normal feels like actual hell;

Best roguelite game I've ever played. The combat and weapons felt satisfying and has a lot of varieties so you can create a lot of playstyle. Story is good imo, tough I don't really care that much. Every death hasn't felt punishing or frustrating so far I play the game. Music and sound is also good. Nice artstyle. 10/10
Real nice, I have died to the same boos for maybe a dozen times now and I still dont feel bored or nitpicky. Genuinely cant find a single bad thing about this game personally, not even a small one.

If you enjoy good games, play this. If you enjoy art, play this. If you enjoy a good story, play this. If you like good music, play this. If you like lovable characters, play this. If you want a good challenge, play this. If you like games with cross-save so that you don't have to start all over on a different platform (which explains my playtime and achievements on here), play this.

Its never to late to say, but one of my favorite game of all time. Since early access i fell in love with this game. The concept, the music, and the game play is phenomenal and even to this day i still feel the love and appreciation they put into this game.

Such a cool game. Its perfect in every way story, art, gameplay, equipments, replayability, difficulty level. This game will always stay in my pc. In case of bugs, very rarely it crashes out to desktop when in loading screen, but its not a big deal because the progression is saved.
Beautiful game. Beautiful character designs. Incredible story. I could replay this game again and again and never get tired of it.

the controls and movement were buttery smooth. I love the synergies you can make with different weapons and how creative you can get. this game is pretty challenging but not to the point where it feels unfair. I have a mac (might as well be a potato) and this runs pretty well which surprised me considering the stunning art and good graphics. in conclusion this is a great game, would highly recommend if you like rouge-like bullet hells with a good challenge where you can make game breaking builds and synergies.

Very fun game, havent played a lot of Roguelike games but this was a very good introduction to the genre. Amazing music, interesting characters, fun dialogue and the combat is incredibly fun and satisfying!
The best rogue-like I've ever played (until Hades II released). A must-play if you enjoy rogue-like games and dungeon crawlers. Some of the best artistic direction and voice acting in gaming.

I sat on this game for almost 4 years, never played. Took a day off work and thought, "Hey maybe I should play this, I'll get an hour or so in and see what's what." Genuinely, sat my ass in my chair and played for 10 hours straight, instantly addicted. Next day I played, nearly beat it, and was so disappointed in myself that I couldn't that I dreamed about beating the final boss in a grand struggle; save the pins and needles in my hands from shoving my elbows into my armrests. The last time I did this with a game was Mount and Blade: Warband about 13 years ago. Immediately addicting, gorgeous art and dialogue, and such a polished feel. I used to think I hated roguelites; I'm entering my love-hate era.

I finally got my mom back from the surface, and now I can escape the Underworld as many times as I want. Life’s been pretty good down here lately — not much to complain about. At this point, I’m just collecting ambrosia so I can keep courting Meg. 10/10 game.

This was the roguelike that made the genre *click* for me personally. It is certainly the easier side of the genre but it acts as a fantastic gateway for it, especially with such a beautiful art style. This game made me go back to Enter The Gungeon and The Binding of Isaac and understand them properly. I look forward to finally getting around to play the sequel to this phenomenal game.

I never thought I’d platinum this game, but after quitting it past the 20h I came back and its depth completely hooked me 'till I couldn’t stop playing. I had to force myself to put it down, as it kept me engaged until the very end.

Hades is one of the best roguelikes I've ever played. The graphics are fantastic, and the optimization is impeccable. Movement and combat are pure pleasure—demanding, yet incredibly satisfying. Zero glitches, and the price is absolutely reasonable. I love the way rougelike's genre is constructed. I love playing for a hundred time gathering secret stuff or making a crazy build around the stuff I get in this particular round. The infinity of this game is captivating and addictive so Imma just rate this game in similar way -> ∞/10

Man, people love this game. And I feel like an idiot posting a negative review, but I just can't get into it. I am a HUGE fan of Transistor, but I just could not get this game to be fun for me. I found the rogue-like mechanics to be just a little too punishing, the RNG a little too random, progression just a little too difficult, and I never really found something that made it "click" for me. I'm not normally a twitchy-platformer type gamer, so I had hesitations going in, but I made it through Basition and SO many people love this game and Transistor was SO good I decided to give it a try. It turned out my instincts were right. If you're not into twitchy rouge-like games that - while "fair" - are still punishingly hard, you probably won't like this one, either.

A genuine fun dive into hell itself. Detailed environments and frustrating enemies. Love the gameplay, story alike and would recommend to anyone wanting something special that's quick to pick up and put down. Much to unlock in both lore and combat.

I've spent so much time in this game, I really like it. It's a bit hard for me to defeat Hades in due time, but I have so much fun completing everything else. And Cerberus is so cute!! Recommended 100%.

Awesome game. I'm an old gamer so I can't run like the pros especially the ones who have spent over 200 hours on this game but I still manage to play this till finish and even play a couple with heat. The longer you play the more you definitely can get better. I wanted to play more but my game bugged out where I can't get Artemis boons in encounters. Only from Chiron or the trial boons where you pick either or. Since I can't give her the gift to make sure she appears I can't do good builds that requires Artemis. I really don't feel like starting again from the beginning. Still, this is a freaking awesome game!
A great game. Entertaining, informative, and addictive. Only gripe is that the game crashes sort of often and you will lose your progress on that run.

Love it. Even though I'm more of a tactical/RPG type of person. It just did everything really well. I still get excited listening to the soundtrack. Went in blind. Gradually learning the world and game mechanics was a smooth, great experience.

If you DON'T like roguelikes, you will likely enjoy it (based on other reviews). If you have experience in roguelikes, you will probably NOT enjoy it. Don't buy it just because of the hype (it's a mystery). Hades really puts the LITE in roguelite. The art is great. It's the best part for me. The story is... I don't know, I didn't finish it. Lore is given in tiny bits of dialogue after each run. While it's nice to have a lot of voiced lines, it's just too much filler. From what I've seen, there's not much intrigue either. Gameplay gets boring after several hours. There are fixed room layouts with the same enemies, very little gameplay variation. The most you can do is try different builds, but they all function mostly the same (basic button mashing). After completing one almost-full run, I just couldn't force myself to do it again. And from what I've heard, you have to do 10+ complete runs just to get the full story. P.S. Rant: Honestly, I'm sick of everyone talking about roguelikes. It's my favourite game genre and Hades is kinda giving it a bad name. "If you don't like it, it's because roguelikes aren't for you." "It's grindy, but roguelikes are supposed to be grindy." No, guys, roguelikes (or lites) are NOT SUPPOSED to be grindy or boring! That's the whole point of being replayable! I have hundreds of hours in other roguelikes, but Hades isn't it.
All around Classic arcade style game; great story and leveling mechanics. Excited for the second one all around great job 10 out of 10!

One of the best roguelites in existence, even as such, terribly, terribly excruciatingly redundant. Even after 30 hours in, I am still nowhere near the "true" ending, and fighting bone hydra even one more time feels like a waste of life. I'll give it an upvote for the artists, who did a beautiful job, and grant everyone else the grace of leaving it at that.
First few runs are fine, but when you get enough grasp of the boons and mirror enhancements it becomes addictive. I completed it in 2022 and now I'm completing it again and it's just as good.

So it's a good game. Probably. The artstyle is great. Definitely. I heard that it is a roguelike even for people who hate roguelikes. And that was a lie. I don't like boss runbacks, ok? This is like one huge 45 min runback. I could list everything I don't like about this game. But it would be just a list of roguelite tropes. But every time you unlock one line of dialogue or something like that. So it is a good roguelite for people who like roguelites.

I went blind coming back from other Supergiant Games and this one took me by surprise. It is a roguelite, so by nature it is grindy. Although in theory you can beat it at the first try, most players will play dozens of runs before beating the final boss and they will repeat even more for true endings, and unlockables. However, Hades differences between runs feel fairly minor. Updates are boring, most of them are small improvements in health or damage, poison vs critical damage, etc. Enemies feel to have too much life and need plenty of button mashing. And unlock new things takes too many runs. If you do not mind repetition and grind, this might be for your. Otherwise avoid.

This is hands down the best rogue-lite game I've ever played. The art style is so gorgeous (I want to eat it) and the story is very catchy and exciting. The interactions and dialogues are never once the same - which, mad props to the devs on that, usually the dialogues on every other game becomes pretty repetitive and I am amazed by the fact that this game is very well done in that regard (just like in almost every other way). I've only encountered one bug but it's not gameplay critical. The gameplay itself it's never the same either, making it more and more difficult it's what marks this game as the very best on it's gender. Kudos to the devs and if you haven't played this game yet, I encourage you to give it a try! I assure you, u won't be disappointed.

Fast, crisp gameplay that supports different styles and approaches. I was particularly impressed by the difficulty curve. Punishing, yet fair, and even when you fail you still feel like you've made progress. Great artwork, enjoyable story and characters.
great game, love the greek mythology aspect and how big it is, i have beaten it a lot of times and i still have things to do in it. 10/10
this game is good if you really enjoy rogue likes but its just too grindy and repetitive for me. characters, story, art, and combat are all very very good
this game has good combat and a good storyline. I like greek mythology and it sums it up very well. i found myself looking forward to meeting and talking to new npcs

I understand why this game is voted as one of the best indie games ever made from the visuals, gameplay, sound design and voiceovers but i find this game very boring. For me the game didnt really pull me in and make me feel like awww this game is amazing or make me have the urge to come back day after day. I was able to get 30 hours of gameplay but i think i am done with this game.
Third playthrough of this game (on other consoles and such) and it doesn't get old. Great action roguelike, one of the best out there.

Really fun gameplay loop. character interactions are really entertaining and the voice acting is so nice with the OST! scaling difficulties make it a fun gameplay loop and really keeps it from getting stale!
Great game, plays amazing on steamdeck. Captures rogue-like essence perfectly. Great story, voice acting, visuals, you will see whether you like the game or not after only a few runs.
The game is frustrating and repetitive, but the variation of the areas keeps your interest following on with the adventure.
A very humorous and refreshing take on the Greek pantheon with rock-solid mechanics, flashy visuals and intense and engaging game-play.

I feel like I learned something about myself, playing this game. Masterclass in game design. Thanks for the story and memories. Can't wait to move on to Hades II (once I'm happy with my achievements) xx

Gave this game a revisit after playing Hades 2 extensively, and it still holds up well to this day. General gameplay loop is frantic and chaotic, with every run feeling different. It's one of the more accessible rouge likes out there, with various difficulty options if you want to crank up the heat or keep things on an easier scale. The art and design of the game is downright amazing, with great character designs and memorable environments. Also features one of the best OSTs I've had the pleasure listening to. I do find the plot here superior to the second game. It has lower stakes, but I found myself more personally invested with Zagreus's story and wanted to find out more with each completed run. I still highly recommend getting this game, it's aged well and is a nice gateway to the roguelike genre.

This is both a really good game and a bore. There's no issue with the difficulty, just with the rate that you earn currency. It would also really be helped by more variation and more innovative enemy attacks. I'm torn on whether to recommend this because it's really good for a few hours, or to not recommend it due to it being a tiresome grind.

My Favorite Game :) - S Thank you, Supergiant! You guys did an amazing job! - the gameplay, the story, the art Hades is one of the main reasons why I got into single player games. This game really showed me that video games are a form of art The only objective downside is that the game has content for ~40-50 hours, but true ending requires ~80 hours. I really hope they fixed that in the second part

Incredible game. Yes, it is not the best roguelite, it does not have in depth mechanics or replayability like The Binding of Isaac or Slay the Spire, but what it does have is incredibly satisfying combat, great story, likeable characters, amazing soundtrack, perfect art and countless hours of fun. And I think that makes up for it. As someone who loves Greek mythology, I would absolutely recommend playing this. 9.5/10

[h1]“Supergiant Game’s first take on making a heavy action roguelite game. Can it break out into the surface or should it be put in the deepest pits of Tartarus?”[/h1] [hr][/hr] [h2]Presentation and Narrative[/h2] - Supergiant Game’s take of the Greek Mythos is a great one. - Beautiful looking Graphics. Art is great. Movesets are easily making every enemy move and reaction readable. - Even though this is a roguelite game, the House of Hades always seems lively with new dialogue each time you visit. This make this game feel really alive. I don’t know how they have done it but I am really impressed! - Music is Great. Not just the music too, the songs as well. - Sound Design is superb and I really like it as well. [hr][/hr] [h2]Gameplay[/h2] - Addictive Hack and Slash Gameplay - Amazing Gameplay Loop. - The mix of your Boons, Weapons and even different aspects of your weapons can make every run unique. - Once I’m in a run, I’m suddenly in a trance where I don’t even notice how the time flies.. I once played until 4am and I had work the same day! - Playing with a Controller is Highly Recommended. I played this mainly on a controller across all weapons. (yes, even with Adamant Rail) [hr][/hr] [h2]Technicality and Value[/h2] - You can see how Supergiant Games learn from their previous games, You can see the influence of Pyre, Transistor, and Bastion into the making the game. Learning from their past games. - Goes Cheap on Sale! - Great Regional Pricing - Rated Platinum on the Steam Deck! [h1]FINAL SCORE: [b]🌕🌕🌕🌕🌕 - 5/5[/b][/h1]

I don't really like action roguelites, but Hades is the exception. Dense with rich dialogue, an amazing soundtrack, great art direction, all neatly revolving around its captivating core gameplay loop. Only real complaint is that it sometimes feels like you're drip-fed the interactions with NPCs, where to advance relevant dialogue another run must be attempted to refresh and advance their quest.

If you love Greek mythology AND dungeon games, this is perfect for you! I wish I had discovered it sooner: banging soundtrack, beautiful art, fun mechanics, and awesome character lore. Every run is different, so you won't get sick of playing through the game again and again. Highly recommend and will be buying Hades 2 next!

Just absolutely one of my favourite games of all time. Gameplay is fast and fun, the characters are great, the music wonderful. It's a surprisingly involved take on Greek mythology. But most of all, the story, if you see enough of it, is deeply moving. The real trick, you see, isn't to escape from the place you're trapped in, it's to work hard to make things better where you are, and forge strong relationships with the people around you. It is in your power to turn your Hell into your home. (This game came out during the Covid-19 pandemic, which is somewhat relevant to the impact such a message had for me.)
I don't like roguelikes/roguelites and yet I spent almost 70 hours with this game. I think that says it all.
Greek mythology AND a rogue-like? both the progression and story are amazing and i also really like the God-mode since it can help with my skill issue, this game is just straight up peak
It's a bit too grindy, I got bored and idk if Im gonna finish it, but it's ok to buy on sale

The game is good to play, it is good to play this game , because it is a good game ,when play this game it feel good to play,hence this game is good game to play.so to conclude the game is a good game and the game is good. Another point to add is that this game is a good game,The game so good it is a good game.
9/10 - RNG-Based Game (SMH). Thanks for the God Mode Setting, it saves a lot of time grinding the game for 100% completion for players like me who dont have- that much time playing the game.

One of the best roguelites of all time. But the game gets very annoying and repetitive the more you play because theres only one route, and it gets super grindy if you want to get the epilogue. The gameplay is great but my hands start hurting after a couple of runs because of how button mashy it is. The art, characters and story are all great tho.
I don't usually play dungeon crawlers but this game really pulled me in with its artstyle and story ! Loved it! Onto Hades 2!
Just completed the game after 116 hours. 32 heat, all achievements, 103 escape attempts. I think I'm done. This is one of the best game I have ever played.
Hades is an old formula refreshed for the current days, the game is beautiful, characters have a huge charisma and the gameplay is really fun. It is an outlier, for today's days even being so simple.

Simple, cool and fun round-based game, its like God of War Valhalla. I am giving a thumbs down because the game SIFU plays similarly but is 10x better. SIFU did not get the recognition it deserved. Play that instead.
Great game with awesome voice acting and an interesting enough story/dialogue to keep you engaged. Extremely re-playable, each run is short enough that you keep coming back.
This game has a unique and creative story. 94 hours and I'd keep playing this game over and over just to uncover more of the story. Highly recommended.

Great game, great music, great story telling. Im not much of a dungeon crawler, but I do enjoy collecting things so I went into each run as a 'I want to stockpile this currency' and I was able to unlock things as I soldiered through. The character designs are cool and I love the different weapon choices to suit different playstyles.

Such a great game. the way the story is connected with the game play is amazing and the characters are really interesting and well written. one of my favourite games. 10/10. i just need more of it. if only hades 2 existed.
amazing game, will keep you in for a long time, pretty difficult but not enough to ruin the expirerience for you. not to expensive either. 10/10 game

fun fact: this was the only game before hades ii came out actually like: - art style goes so unbelievably hard - voice acting so beautiful and soft and sultry and british because theyre greek obviously - literally look at all of the characters - [spoiler] threesome [/spoiler] - dionysus - the music - the gameplay is so so rewarding - dying is rarely actually disappointing - gameplay is f u n and has yet to get repetitive because the builds are so variable - god mode dislike: - can be confusing to understand how to build character trust, but if you just play the game enough you're good - thats literally it

One of the best games I have ever had the opportunity to play if you can buy it on sale for 7$ you will enjoy it but this game is easily worth its full price almost done with the story at around 25 hours but I still see another 25 hours before I feel done.

[h1][b]One of my favorites:[/b] Hades[/h1] [b]Hades[/b] was a bit of an odd duck in my Steam library. I remember buying it way back when and liking it quite a bit, but I couldn't really recall any specifics. In fact, I was a bit apprehensive to try it again, since I'm generally not a huge fan of roguelikes, and my reflexes aren't exactly what they used to be. As it turns out, my fears were completely unfounded. The story follows Zagreus, the son of the titular Hades, as he attempts to escape the Underworld and reunite with his mother, Persephone. Along the way, he'll face perilous foes, meet unexpected allies, and, little by little, unravel the mystery of his origins. While the plot isn't particularly intricate, what it lacks in complexity, it more than makes up for by how well it's integrated with the gameplay. Each escape attempt is an opportunity, not just to get a deeper understanding of the game mechanics, but also to interact with the NPCs and learn more about them and their stories. Luckily, Zagreus isn't going at it alone - the various gods of Olympus are invested in his journey, and will offer their aid in the form of boons, which give Zagreus various active and passive abilities. These upgrades are plentiful enough to make each run meaningfully different, and more strategically-minded players are sure to find a whole bevy of powerful synergies. The whole thing is further expanded by the six weapons at your disposal, each of which has its own play style and a slew of modifications that will help you fine-tune them to your preference. The combat is buttery smooth and incredibly satisfying. It's also very well balanced (at least at the standard difficulty setting, but more on that later), so even someone like me, who isn't all that skilled with the pixel-perfect hack-and-slash gameplay, can still get in the groove and enter that flow state. Of course, no game is perfect, and the same certainly applies to Hades. As a roguelike (Or is it roguelite? I can never tell.), Hades has all the inherent flaws of the genre, the first of which is randomness. As you progress through an escape attempt, you'll get a reward for each room you clear. However, considering that these rewards are random, you don't really have that much control over how your run is going to turn out. Sure, most of the time, you get a choice of a couple of rooms you can visit next, with previews of the rewards helping inform your decision. Still, more often than not, you're choosing the lesser of two evils (especially on higher difficulties, where you have to carefully plan for synergies to have any hope of defeating the bosses). You can also unlock the option to reroll the reward in an upcoming room, but getting that much darkness can take quite a while and you only get a limited number of uses per run. After you successfully complete a few runs, you'll get the option to further tweak your experience by playing with a slew of difficulty modifiers. These are instrumental in acquiring rare resources, like titan blood, diamonds, and ambrosia, since these only drop the first time you defeat a boss on a given difficulty level. However, I found that the more I tuned up the difficulty, the more likely I was to default to the same tried and tested build over and over again. This is a pretty big deal, since it takes a fun but challenging hack-and-slash and turns it into an absolute slog as you're trying to chase the perfect combination of boons. The presentation is absolutely stunning. The Underworld and its denizens are rendered in beautiful hand-drawn illustrations. The levels are incredibly polished and show a fantastic level of attention to detail - candles will snuff out as you walk over them and relight as you move away, random shades milling about will react to Zagreus destroying various pots and columns, and you'll even see the name of one of the bosses change after Zagreus decides to give it a nickname. The voice acting is superb, with the return of many of the Supergiant regulars, such as Logan Cunningham (who lends his baritone to about half of the male characters), Darren Korb, Christopher Saphire, and Jamie Landrum. The music is pretty solid, as it successfully nails the "Greek" vibe and drives the combat. However, it does feel a bit underused, since the more noticeable, fast-paced combat tracks only pop up here and there. The most important lesson I came away with after playing Hades is to know when to quit. No, I didn't get all the achievements, or even unlock all of the dozens of furniture upgrades for the House, but who cares? With 100+ hours of fun, it's more than enough, and the fact that I was still finding new details and discovering new synergies after more than a hundred runs shows just how much bang you get for your buck. Hades is an absolute must-have, and I can't wait to sink my teeth into part two.
