For years as an Apex player, I was keenly aware of the Titanfall sect of the fanbase who loudly demanded a Titanfall 3. I thought it was just nostalgia, or brand-induced Stockholm Syndrome where someone just *had* to root for an underdog. I was wrong. I get it now. I went into Titanfall 2 only expecting Apex movement, and it not only delivered on that, but on a thousand other things I hadn't realised I'd been wanting for years now. In 2025, I played Doom the Dark Ages. It was the first time playing modern DOOM I thought "they have the secret sauce, they've nailed a modern take on the godfather of FPS", and I had such a good time with that, so much so I rank it as my favourite FPS campaign since Halo 2. I STILL maintain that Doom TDA is that good, despite its dismal post-launch content, but man oh man, Titanfall 2 is AS GOOD, and it came out 9 years before TDA. Much like how you can spot the DNA of Half-Life, Halo and MGS in a lot of modern games, I can identify where Titanfall 2 introduced and innovated and recall many derivatives in the year since that I always felt were good, but missed that secret sauce. I now know why that sauce was missing: they were imitating something that came before, something that did its job so well everything ever-after will always feel derivative. It is to FPS what RE4 Remake is to the action-horror formula CAPCOM has laboured for 20+ years to perfect. An excellently paced campaign, with Mech combat up there with the King of Kings, Armored Core: Fires of Rubicon. Incredible, HOPEcore soundtrack that leaves you smiling through set-piece after set-piece. A roster of characters oozing personality, even if the majority were written in such a way to lead into the next game. BT is the greatest Mech of all time, with a voice that echoes Peter Cullen's Optimus Prime but a cheeky wit that puts him more alongside the sweeter side of GLaDOS. The gunplay is superb, all the weapons I loved in Apex are present as well as some extras, though they feel much better because the game doesn't need to attune itself to a PVP meta. Sound design is eargasm-inducing, controls are fantastic, and optimisation is so good I could play on 1440p with everything maxed out and still keep a locked 144hz WHILE STREAMING to friends. I understand why people clamour for a third game. The late Vince Zampella and his team made something special, and that game being as special as it is makes me glad to play videogames, because this is what I play for; special experiences you cannot replicate in any other medium, with raw gameplay and no intrusive modern-game-isms interrupting you every five seconds to demand you *feel* for something. Titanfall 2 isn't the game everyone wanted back then, which is why it failed, but it's the game we all needed. Frankly, gamers don't deserve good games like this: they pursue dopamine from live-service trash while jerking to ethots and farming anime girls in Gacha phone games. This game is a lovingly crafted labour of love that truly innovated the long-stagnant FPS genre, and YOU shunned its love and turned it away. I feel the pain of a loss that never was, knowing this won't ever get a sequel, and even if Modern EA greenlit one, Vince and the visionaries behind it are long gone. 10/10. A genuine masterpiece of gameplay innovation, even with the Online being neglected and abandoned by EA who wants to bleed you dry in Battlefield that gets worse with each entry. Loved this game. I felt like a kid again. Keeping it installed forever.

I highly recommend Titanfall 2 for players aged 16 and up. I honestly don’t have any real negatives to say about this game. It was an incredible experience from start to finish. The storytelling is one of its strongest aspects, especially following Jack Cooper. Without going into spoilers, the journey he takes alongside his Titan, BT 7274, is both exciting and emotional. Their bond really stands out and adds depth to the entire campaign. BT was easily my favorite character, and the connection between pilot and Titan made every mission feel meaningful. Each mission is carefully crafted, with detailed storytelling, impressive graphics, and smooth, well designed animations. The variety in gameplay keeps things fresh, and the pacing never feels dull. Whether you are playing casually or attempting a speedrun, there are plenty of fun challenges and rewarding moments to discover. From a technical standpoint, the game performed great on my setup. I experienced little to no lag, which made the overall gameplay feel smooth and immersive. All in all, Titanfall 2 is one of the best games I have ever played. It delivers a powerful story, engaging gameplay, and a memorable cast of characters. I would easily give it a 10 out of 10.

Titanfall 2 surprised me in the best way. I just finished the hard difficulty campaign and every moment felt polished and memorable. The game is linear but it never feels restrictive because each level introduces new mechanics, new weapons and fresh ideas. Every time I picked up a new weapon or gained a new ability, it felt like I was playing a different character which kept the experience exciting from start to finish. The movement is incredibly smooth and fast. Wall-running, sliding and switching between Pilot and Titan gameplay make combat dynamic and satisfying. The relationship between Cooper and BT-7274 is also a strong highlight. The story is simple but effective and the emotional moments land well without dragging the pacing down. Performance was solid on my laptop at 1080p low settings averaging around 35–40 FPS, which made the experience very playable. Visually the game still looks impressive and level design is consistently creative. The only downside is that the campaign feels short to me. I would have loved a longer story maybe around 10 hours, because the gameplay is so enjoyable. Still the quality is high throughout with no filler. Titanfall 2 is absolutely worth playing. I really hope we get a sequel someday.

I fear my experience with [i]Titanfall 2[/i] got tainted by expectation bias. To me, this was like an average buddy cop movie except the buddy is a mecha robot. It does have fun movement and there are about 2-3 exceptional levels in the game, however, if you suffer from expectation bias heavily, I would try to keep them minimal. You might have a better time with the game.

This was an extremely well-complimented FPS when it released, for its innovative use of parkour, and the addition of mech battles, and years later it is still a very solid experience that doesn't feel outdated. The story and soundtrack are average, but it's fine because the gameplay carries the game perfectly and you won't wish for much else. Honing my skills in the game was very rewarding, even though I haven't quite spent that long in the game. The multiplayer is especially fun, though since it's a very old game it isn't easy to get matches (there are ways to make it easier, but it's not vanilla). It was also a very solid achievement hunting project, I got 100% in just under 20 hours, and I am proud of it. It's not RNG dependant and can even be done with very little help from guides (I only used help to find all map secrets, but they aren't too hard to find by yourself). It's also almost all related to the campaign, and multiplayer achievements are super simple and can be done in a single match if you're lucky. Especially considering this game made history - and that I, as a future game designer, want to know of said history - Titanfall 2 was a solid purchase, and I honestly had a blast. I only wish I had friends that also play it.

I cannot recommend this game enough. There are no games with a better movement system than Titanfall. Ultrakill comes close, but Titanfall 2 ultimately is crowned movement shooter king. I bought this game for the campaign, but stayed for the multiplayer. There is quite the variety of multiplayer games, all of them amazing. The community of Titanfall 2 is very wholesome, with only a few toxic people here and there. Win or loose, most people will say gg, and accept a loss without crying. When a multiplayer match begins, everyone starts out on an even playing field, all with fairly balanced weapons. As the match progresses, and you get a few kills and farm a few grunts, you can activate your special skill usually giving you a small advantage in a shoot-out. At this point, the score will be leaning towards one team or the other. Soon the first titan is called in, which can quickly flip the scales, giving the team a huge advantage. Soon after that, more titans are called in, evening the playing field somewhat and drastically changing the pace of the game, forcing you to change your playstyle with it. Now the game turns into a Hero shooter, with the Seven different Titan variants each encourage a different playstyle, all of them with their unique strengths and weaknesses, which will all change depending on the map you are playing. Titanfall 2 truly is one-of-a-kind. If you haven't bought it already, you should. But only on sale. Despite being overshadowed by a different major game on release, and abandoned by the devs, Titanfall still maintains a regular, and devoted playerbase, though I think most players are on console. AND THE CAMPAIGN. DO NBOT FORGET THE CAMPAIGN. Don't get me started on the campaign. Easily comperable to Halo's campaign, but very unique at the same time. It isn't half as long as Halo, but it is still incredible. I will never forget the ending. A banger ending that will stay with me forever. If you are even mildly interested in Titanfall 2, you should buy it. We need more people asking Respawn for Titanfall 3 :3

It’s a good game, but it will probably never have a sequel because Titanfall 3 wouldn’t be able to match Titanfall 2. The main story of Titanfall 2 set a very high bar, especially with the bond between the player and BT, and it would be hard to recreate that emotional connection in a new game. Every year, players’ expectations grow as technology improves, but that also makes it harder to innovate enough. Titanfall 3 would need a lot of new gameplay ideas to stand out, not just better graphics. If Titanfall 3 were released as a $60 AAA game, I think there’s a high chance it could fail — maybe 9 out of 10 times because it would struggle to meet those expectations. The universe has moved forward by around 15–30 years, and during that time, technology has significantly advanced, as seen in Apex Legends. Because of this, things like portals and other high-end technologies have become more common, which could make Titans feel outdated or less relevant compared to these newer innovations. Because of this rapid technological growth, Titans could end up feeling outdated or even useless compared to these newer innovations, which makes it harder for a new Titanfall game to stay true to its original titan-focused gameplay. Maybe the only way it could work is if they separate it and tell the story in a different timeline.

An impossibility is defined as something impossible, or the state of being impossible. This is often used to describe things deemed flukes, singular events, or isolated incidents. Something that will never happen, and can be treated as such. Titanfall 2 is an impossibility. Its future is missing, its past killed. It will never get a sequel, and I think that's a good thing. The mere fact that it exists is nothing short of incredible. Nowhere else can you find a game that feels and plays the way Titanfall 2 does. It's refreshing, exciting, challenging, and rewarding. No advantage is locked behind a paywall. Nothing requires tedious or frustrating work to unlock. No live service. No competitive matchmaking. You can play singleplayer, PvP, or PvE, and all three are entirely satisfying. You can play it alone or with friends and have an absolute blast. You can achievement hunt, challenge yourself to harder difficulties, speedrun, play with friends, try crazy loadouts, hunt camos and upgrades, spin a wheel to pick a gun, do trickshots, the list goes on; and that's all excluding the actual variety of modes and options the game provides for you. Everything you do is progress, and more importantly, it's always so much fun. Even being on the losing side of a game is loads of fun. The game does an amazing job of making you feel engaged, immersed, and really cool, no matter what you're doing. Most games weren't even this good before Titanfall 2 came out, nor do they generally feel this fun today. A third installment would be microtransaction hell, and no other games I've seen have actually hit the mark on what made this game so special. Every part of it is exceptional, and I can't think of any exceptions to that. Games like that are rare, so rare, and deserve every morsel of praise and cherishing they get. If you like FPS games, or vehicle games, or any gun games, or to feel like you're going fast, or big robots, or good story games, or arcade games, or PvP games, or games that just look stunning, or games that give you an adrenaline rush, or games where you send four *ssholes to save the world, take my word, you will enjoy this game. I've been playing since release (originally on PS4), and have since bought seven copies to give to my friends because it's actually that good. And I haven't even mentioned modding. It only gets better. Titanfall 2 is an impossibility. I'm so lucky to have found it, and to be able to play it still, and I'll always be thankful for that. If you're reading this, and you haven't played it, this is your sign. There's a reason this game's community refuses to die, and I'm proud to be part of that.

Score: 3/5 [b]The Good[/b] 1. Visuals, Strong and consistent artistic direction 2. Strong audio/SFX and voice acting, Good music/soundtrack 3. Humor 4. Gameplay. Although the gunplay was a bit worse after playing Apex Legends first, movement is still strong and mechs/guns/explosives feel very impactful/powerful with a decent amount of balanced options. Some of the ammo pickup amounts, along with the quality of the AI combatants, were lacking though. 5. Strong pacing and reasonable game length. New mechanics and gear/weapons/etc. provide some spice as you switch levels or progress into a second half of a few maps. [b]The Bad[/b] 1. Writing is alright, with a moderate amount of predictability and plot armor and annoyances. Setting is goofy, but consistently takes itself just seriously enough that the jokes/humor don't ruin the drama/stakes. Main character is often center of universe. I was bored more than once due to lackluster writing or story beats and turned off my brain until the next gameplay section started. 2. Linearity. Lack of replayability for a story/exploration-focused player (I only played once). Small number of player choices have very limited impact, usually only alternative dialogues. [b]The Unknown[/b] 1. Multiplayer experience. 2. NG+

I've been a fan of core team behind Respawn since Call of Duty 2 came out. As Infinity Ward they created my favourite games of all times till even today (CoD 2, CoD 4, CoD MW2). After a scandal with Activision core team left IW and became Respawn Entertainment (sadly without Jason West). First Titanfall was pretty ambition game with a lot of incredible and fun ideas but sadly it was barebone. As a person who has a lot of experience with basically all of their games I can say that Titanfall 2 was two steps away from being theirs Opus Magnum. Unlike the first game, sequel has a Singleplayer Campaign which has a total of 8+1 levels. Each of them plays incredibly fun and unqiue gameplaywise. I'm 100% sure everyone will like them. The only problem I have with it - it's too short. When I finished Campaign, it wasn't enough for me, I wanted MORE. Mainly because of that the story is pretty simple and only two charcaters will shine - the protagonist and BT. Overall it's good but Respawn made MW2 campaign back in 2009 so I expected from them something better. Multiplayer is where this game trully shines. Sequel fixed and improved almost everything what was wrong with the first game - Time-to-Kill is shorter, more weapons which are very distinct, Titan and Pilot classes are well balanced and each of them is also very unique, no more expendable card system but only support card. The best part is how well everything is put together. The gameplay flow, the way Titans, Pilots and even bots are fighting each other on the one battlefield, the environment, the guns, the pilot classes, the titan classes, the wallruing and parkour. So many mechanics put together and everything just works perfectly with each other. On the negative notes - the maps. The first map had 15 on release and 9 more in DLC. [b]Titanfall 2 Review[/b] Among the behemoths of the FPS genre, Titanfall 2 stands on a league of its own. [list] [b] Gameplay [/b] [*][u]Movement[/u] - First and foremost, the movement handles like a [i]dream[/i]. Wallrunning feels intuitive, sliding feels visceral, and air-strafing feels surreal, resulting in one of the most satisfying movement mechanics I’ve had the pleasure experiencing. Once you master it, you can pretty much zoom across the map at mach speed. [*][u]Weapons[/u] - The guns carry real weight and delivers a punch. You’ve got a wide selection of weapons to pick. From pistols to revolvers—ARs, SMGs, Shotguns, Railguns, Snipers, Grenade Launchers—there’s even a gun that shoots Ball Lightnings! [*][u]Tacticals[/u] - Tacticals are definitely one of the best features of the game. They are the Titanfall Equivalent of classes and each one offers abilities and utilities, including: Grappling Hook, Invisibility, Legal Wall Hack, Shadow Clone Jutsu, Dimensional Border Crosser, Crack Lord, and lastly, Brain Damage. [*][u]Titans[/u] - Anybody who’s seen the trailer or any youtube videos knows what a titan is. Titans are like the Assault Helicopter in OG Call of Duty. Only this time, you’re gripping the flight stick. You get to control a 100 ton hunk of junk packed with enough ordnance to nuke a town and wreak havoc across the battlefield. In multiplayer, you can pick one to use in the match. Each one is special and are genuinely one of the most endearing robot companions in gaming. [b]Campaign[/b] [*][u]Theme[/u] - At its core, the story is about fighting for the things you hold dear and a home close to heart. Classic. [*][u]Story[/u] - The story follows Rifleman Jack Cooper and his trusty robot companion BT as they fight the good fight against the IMC, an evil human space empire destroying their home. A real solid campaign. [*][u]Writing and Pacing[/u] - The campaign is packed with a lot of meaningful characters, good and bad. When you play Jack, you really get a feel for why the militia is fighting. BT and Jack’s relationship is the highlight of the campaign. BT, despite being a robot, has the personality of a dumb but loyal kid. The conversations you have with him are short yet endearing. It really is the small moments that pull at your heartstrings. [b]Multiplayer[/b] [*][u]Matches[/u] - There are a variety of multiplayer matches you can choose. The most common one you’ll find are Attrition Matches, where you and your team fight against the opposing team in a medium-sized map with the goal of winning the most points. Other matches include Pilots vs. Pilots, Titan Brawl, and Free-For-All. [b]Technical[/b] [*][u]Visuals[/u] - Despite being nearly a decade old, Titanfall 2 sports outstanding visuals comparable to those of games today. The real meat is in the Art direction, going for the stylistic, neon and bright colors. Maps like The Beacon, Exoplanet, and Firebase Kodai are one of the best maps in the game. [*][u]Performance[/u] - I play this game on an Acer Nitro V 16 Gaming Laptop and it runs perfectly fine, often reaching over 200-300 frames per second at Max Graphics. [/list] The reason I consider Titanfall 2 worlds apart from other FPS titles is that it got a lot of things to offer and a lot of things it got right. Movement, mechanics, a killer campaign—you’re telling me I can run on walls, fire a railgun, slip dimensions, ride a gundam, [i]FLY[/i] a gundam, go toe to toe with a titan and survive, fly through the map at the speed of light, and all of this happens in one game? Just hook me up with crack, I won’t know the difference. Overall. Titanfall is an amazing game. A real lightning in a bottle.

I finally played Titanfall 2, and yeah… they really don’t make games like this anymore. The campaign surprised me the most. I went in expecting a decent shooter story, but the dynamic between Jack and BT ended up being the highlight of the whole game. It’s simple, but it works so well. BT isn’t just a machine you’re piloting — it actually feels like a partner, and the way their relationship develops over the course of the game makes the story hit harder than I expected. Gameplay-wise, it’s just fun the entire time. The movement is smooth, fast, and satisfying. Wall-running, sliding, chaining everything together — it never gets old. And the game constantly switches things up with different level mechanics, so it never feels repetitive. There’s one mission in particular that plays with time in a really clever way, and it’s easily one of the most memorable levels I’ve played in any shooter. The pacing is also really solid. The campaign isn’t super long, but it doesn’t waste time either. Every mission feels different, and it keeps introducing new ideas without dragging anything out. Visually, the game still holds up really well. The environments are varied, and the Titan combat adds that extra scale that makes everything feel bigger. My only real annoyance wasn’t even the game itself — it’s dealing with the EA launcher. Having to go through that just to play can be frustrating, and it takes away a bit from an otherwise smooth experience. Overall, it’s an amazing campaign that mixes great gameplay with a surprisingly strong story. It’s one of those games that reminds you how good single-player shooters can be when everything comes together. Definitely worth playing if you haven’t already.

Stellar Campaign. Probably one of the most memorable I have played, alongside The Last of Us, Metro 2033 and STALKER. The story telling is beyond good and the gameplay is fun, creative and unique. Titanfall 2 is a solid game with an interesting setting and completely new and exciting world. The story is simple yet the world it takes place is complex and well made which requires the player to understand the lore of titanfall its various factions and the conflicts, for a game which looks like a simple mech shooter on the surface it has a lot of depth. The campaign is short but full of quality. It is fun from the starting to end it does not deviate from main story at all and there are sections in the game which play and feel completely different from what you have been playing with the help of new devices and class of weapons that you find as you progress. The gameplay is absolutely fun and amazing the movement is really well done it feels very satisfying so is the gunplay mechanics. The graphics look insane in the game although the models of actual human characters feel basic and make you feel its age for an otherwise gorgeous game which even lives up today. The game performance is amazing and no complaints. The multiplayer is decent but has only few players available but thankfully the servers have actual people trying to enjoy the game rather than hackers and cheaters TITANFALL HAS A VERY INTRESTING AND COMPLEX STORY AND GREAT WORLD BUILDING WHICH ELEVATES THE PERFECT GAMEPLAY. OVERALL-9/10

Matchmaking in multiplayer is absolutely broken ... though it's a miracle to have an active community after almost a decade ... PvE mode's a hidden gem, where I've spent over half of all my time. Replayed Titanfall 2’s campaign in 2026 and honestly forgot how insanely good it is. The graphics still hold up way better than they have any right to, performance is rock solid, and the movement/combat is just on another level. Everything feels fast, smooth, and satisfying in a way most shooters still don’t nail. Short, tight, no filler just pure quality. Honestly the only downside is how short it is… Still one of the best FPS campaigns ever made.

Titanfall 2 is one of the best FPS games ever made, and it still holds up. The campaign is short but insanely memorable—no filler, just creative missions and a surprisingly emotional story. The movement system is on another level; once you get used to it, every other shooter feels slow and clunky. Titans actually feel meaningful too, not just gimmicks. Multiplayer deserved way more attention than it got. The game was completely screwed by its release window, and you can still feel that today. Honestly, the biggest problem with Titanfall 2 is that it reminds you of what we don’t have: Titanfall 3.

This game holds a special place in my heart. I would definitely recommend it — the price drops to 80–90% off from time to time, so why wouldn't you buy it? The story and The story is like an art piece; it's beautiful and if you give it a chance and some time, I'm sure you'll really enjoy it. OK, you need to play it at least twice to discover everything, and there are even secrets in the voice lines. Sadly, EA has abandoned the game, but the PvE mode is still alive and the PvP matches work, although they take some time as the game has a small but dedicated fan base. In Story Mode, there is a Time Run in the Tutorial Level. After some time, you realise that there is more to it. The movement in this game is still unmatched to this day — it's not even close. It's very complex, but it's good. this game for me is defenetly a 9-10. I also have the game on PS4, and I 100% it.

This game is AMAZING. I usually don't play first-person shooter games, but I absolutely loved Titanfall. The scenery in every mission is absolutely gorgeous and the gameplay is fun as hell. I like how the guns and ammo are dispersed within the levels, and playing as the Titan was easy to get the hang of. The only complaint I have is that there are only nine missions in total, not including multiplayer. I would have loved to see more of the story behind Titanfall, but the game seems to end unexpectedly. I never really got to know any of the characters besides BT-7274 and Jack Cooper, and I didn't understand the motive behind the enemies I was fighting. Granted, I haven't tried multiplayer yet (I'm not a fan of PvP) and I've only beaten the game on easy so far. Nonetheless, this game is definitely worth a try if you're looking for a beautiful and fun first-person shooter or PvP!

I didn’t know a video game could hit me like this. I didn’t know that a shooter could make me feel awe, joy, tension, and that weird, rare satisfaction that comes when every system clicks perfectly. Titanfall 2 didn’t just entertain me—it made me rethink what I expect from games, from stories, and even from myself when I play. First, the story. I can’t tell you plot beats without spoiling, but I can tell you this: it’s smart, it’s emotional, and it’s written with a confidence that most shooters can’t even muster in their loading screens. It treats its characters like real people—yes, in a shooter—and I caught myself caring deeply about their fates. It’s the kind of narrative that doesn’t rely on cheap twists or overblown spectacle; instead, it makes you feel, and that’s a wild thing for a genre I assumed was only about shooting stuff. I laughed. I held my breath. I felt genuinely thrilled in moments I didn’t even think were possible in a first‑person shooter. Then the gameplay hit. It’s fluid in ways that defy physics but somehow feel natural. Wall‑running, double‑jumping, sliding, climbing—movement isn’t just functional, it’s poetry. Every action is kinetic, satisfying, and addictive. You don’t just navigate the world; you dance through it. And then there are the Titans, which are colossal, terrifying, and awe-inspiring, but also deeply satisfying to control. There’s a rhythm here, a push and pull between pilot and mech that’s intoxicating. Every engagement feels like a perfect storm of precision, chaos, and control. I’ve replayed sections just to revel in that feeling. Combat is equally brilliant. Guns feel weighty. Explosions land with authority. Enemies aren’t just targets—they’re challenges that demand thought, speed, and creativity. Every encounter forces you to adapt and rewards ingenuity. And the pacing is insane in the best way—never too frantic, never dull, just the perfect balance to keep you invested. Visually, the game is gorgeous without being showy. Maps are meticulously crafted, giving you verticality, scope, and plenty of spaces to explore your newfound movement abilities. Audio design is spectacular; every mechanical roar, gunshot, and environmental cue is perfectly timed to keep you immersed. You feel the world in a way that transcends what most shooters even attempt. What really hits, though, is how complete the experience feels. The story, the mechanics, the world—they aren’t just thrown together. They resonate. You feel the weight of your actions, the thrill of mastery, the joy of discovery. Playing it, I kept thinking, “This is the kind of game that reminds me why I love gaming.” And I mean it—every hour with Titanfall 2 made me a little more obsessed, a little more alive in ways I didn’t expect. It’s not perfect—no game is—but it feels perfect in those fleeting, breathtaking moments where everything clicks. You finish a mission or a multiplayer match, and you can’t help but sit back, catch your breath, and think, “This is how it’s supposed to feel.” The game doesn’t just give you entertainment—it gives you exhilaration, pride, challenge, and pure, unfiltered fun all at once. I can’t overstate it: Titanfall 2 changed how I see shooters, how I see story in games, and how I see movement and combat design. It’s the kind of experience that leaves you buzzing long after you’ve put the controller down, wondering how anything could possibly feel this good again. It’s more than a game. It’s a revelation.

Titanfall 2 feels like the rare FPS that respects both your time and your skill. Titanfall 2 is one of those games that came out during the futuristic shooter fever, and was one of the last survivors of it's era. Thankfully, it still holds up. Criteria: Story, Gameplay, Progression/Loop, Visuals, Performance/QOL, Side Content/Replay Factor Final Rating: The average between all the ratings. STORY: 5/10 This game's story is by far the weakest aspect. Is it horrible to the point of making the game unplayable? No. Is it ANY good? Also no. This story is the most generic thing you'll ever experience in a game. Titanfall 2's plot is basically if Star Wars met Call of Duty. Big Bad Company is taking over Good Guys planets, Good Guys form a militia to fight Big Bad Company. Big Bad Company has weapon of mass destruction that will destroy Good Guys's planet and kill many Good Guys, so Good Guys must stop Big Bad Company. That's about it. As i said, this doesn't make the game unplayable since the story is barely there. It's just background noise, some random sh1t to give you some context to do the cool stuff in-game. Although the story itself is weak and boring, the gameplay setpieces compensate these weaknesses. For example: That whole time travel/Arc ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was extremely boring storywise. Gameplaywise, however, it was one of the coolest things i've ever seen in a videogame. Basically, the story is completely irrelevant. The only things that somewhat hold it together are the interactions between BT and Cooper. Although Cooper is clearly a blank slate for the player with dialogue "Choices" that don't change anything(John Titanfall), their interactions are pretty cool. GAMEPLAY: 10/10 Titanfall 2 has a gameplay that is perfect for the premise. Satisfying gunplay and movement, sliding, double jumping, ziplining, grappling hooks and, of course, the wall running. Every single action in the game feels responsive and crisp, both as a Pilot and while controlling your Titan. I thought that controlling Titans would be boring, like using tanks in Battlefield or Call of Duty, but i was completely wrong. Pilot gameplay is fast paced and chaotic, while controlling Titans is more strategic. Every single mistake punishes you a lot, but every single right decision is extremely rewarding. The multiplayer modes are also very cool. The idea of having random grunts to shoot and smash as a Titan is perfect for the game's style, and gives an "All-out war" feel that makes everything even more fast paced, since the grunts, Reapers, Fleas and etc can actually kill you and you get meaningful points when you kill them. PROGRESSION/LOOP: 5/10 Another weak aspect of the game. As you can see by my record, i only played five hours of the game so far, and i've already unlocked all the things i wanted. Now, the only things left for me to unlock are sights, some mods that barely change anything and ugly skins. In the campaign, you have these boring collectibles in the form of pilot helmets that i think don't give you anything besides an achievment. The only things you can unlock in the campaign are more loadouts for BT, but that isn't exactly progression, since they are in very linear and obvious paths, literally impossible to miss. Performance/QOL: 10/10 Greatly optmized game. With everything on Ultra, the game runs at a constant and smooth 298 FPS on my PC. Never experienced any bugs or glitches, a miracle, considering that the EA Launcher is a piece of sh1t. Props. Side Content/Replay Factor: 5/10 As mentioned before, the game has little to no content to explore. I beat the entire campaign in just four hours, and i have very few reasons to replay it. Titanfall 2 is carried entirely by the amazing gameplay and graphics, since it doesn't have much substance to it. The multiplayer is fun, but the lack of significant progression doesn't gave too much incentive to really play it that much. Frontier Defense is pretty creative and cool to play, but also suffers from the lack of content. FINAL RATING 7.5/10 Although the game barely has a story and it's content is spread pretty thin, it's still an amazing piece of entertainment. The gameplay and graphics are flawless, and you'll be having a blast when playing. I intend to do 100% of the game and keep playing the multiplayer for a bit longer. If the game is on a good sale, it's a must-have. Very fun game, even with all it's flaws.

I don’t usually write long reviews for games, but Titanfall 2 honestly deserves it. It’s one of those rare games that surprised me in the best possible way. I picked it up expecting a fun shooter, but what I got was a game with an amazing campaign, incredibly smooth gameplay, and one of the most enjoyable multiplayer experiences I’ve had in years. The single-player story is much better than I expected from a shooter like this. You play as Jack Cooper, a rifleman who ends up bonding with a Titan named BT-7274 after his commander dies in battle. What starts as a simple military mission slowly turns into a really emotional journey between a pilot and his Titan. BT isn’t just a machine that you call into battle - he actually feels like a real companion. Throughout the campaign you build a connection with him through dialogue, teamwork, and the situations you go through together. Some moments in the story are surprisingly touching, and by the end of the campaign I was way more invested than I expected. The missions themselves are incredibly creative. Instead of repeating the same shooting gallery over and over again, the game constantly introduces new mechanics. One level has you switching between two timelines in the middle of combat, another takes place in a factory that literally assembles entire buildings while you fight through it. It keeps the campaign feeling fresh the whole time, and I never felt bored or like I was just doing the same thing again and again. The gameplay is where Titanfall 2 really shines. The movement system is fantastic. Running on walls, sliding across the ground, jumping between rooftops, and chaining all those moves together feels incredibly smooth and natural. Once you get the hang of it, you feel almost unstoppable flying across the map. It’s one of those games where simply moving around is fun by itself. And then there are the Titans. Calling down a giant mech in the middle of a battle never gets old. Each Titan has its own abilities and weapons, which makes them feel very different from each other. Some are built for heavy damage, others are more tactical, and learning how to use them properly adds another layer of strategy to the game. The multiplayer is just as impressive. It’s fast, chaotic, and incredibly satisfying once you learn the movement system. Unlike many shooters where players move slowly and fights happen around corners, Titanfall 2 encourages constant motion. Players are running across walls, jumping across buildings, and dropping Titans onto the battlefield. It creates these huge, cinematic battles that feel unlike anything else. What I also like about the multiplayer is that it stays accessible. Even if you’re not the best player in the lobby, you can still contribute by fighting AI enemies, helping your team earn points, and working toward calling down your Titan. That makes the matches feel exciting even when you’re still learning the game. Visually, the game still looks great even years after release. The environments are detailed, the Titan designs are fantastic, and the animations are incredibly smooth. The sound design is also excellent - the heavy footsteps of Titans, the roar of weapons, and the music during intense battles all add a lot to the atmosphere. Overall, Titanfall 2 is easily one of the most underrated shooters ever made. The campaign is creative and emotional, the gameplay is incredibly smooth, and the multiplayer is both intense and fun. It’s the kind of game that reminds you why shooters can still be exciting when developers try something different. If you enjoy fast-paced action, great movement mechanics, and a surprisingly strong story, Titanfall 2 is absolutely worth playing. It’s a game that I still come back to, and every time I do, it reminds me just how special it is.

The game is very good. I've played it several times on all difficulty levels, trying out all the titans and getting all the collectibles. I love the game's story, and it looks great even for how old it is. It never stops being fun, no matter how many times you play it. It's so much fun that I've managed to get all the Steam achievements, something I rarely set out to do. But it was after I finished the story mode and got everything this game had to offer that I decided to try online multiplayer, and that's when I realized that this game has one big problem. It's forgotten. By this I don't mean that it doesn't have players, in fact, it does, but if you're a casual player or a new player, you won't be able to enjoy multiplayer very much because the matchmaking isn't balanced correctly. I've seen multiple times how G60 or G80 players (the highest levels) destroy G3 or G10 players, or even the newest ones, and then proceed to mock and insult them, using the classic “skill issues” excuse. And yes, of course it's skill issues. Casual and new players aren't going to devote 500 hours of their lives to this game like others do. They just want to have fun, which they can't do when there's such a stark imbalance between players. In my opinion, this is mainly the fault of the developer, as there is no way to regulate this “imbalance” between high-level and low-level players, which is why I strongly recommend that you do not enter multiplayer if you are a beginner and just want to relax and have fun. Now, if you're a tryhard player and want to devote a thousand hours to multiplayer, go ahead, but there are many others like you who won't stop insulting you in multiplayer (not to mention that the game tends to have hackers in matches more often than you think). Personally, I would recommend enjoying the game in single-player mode as much as you can, because it's great. Also enjoy border defense because it's a lot of fun. And if you're looking to have fun, don't go into multiplayer mode, because you'll only find aggressive, annoying G60s and above, and a lot of frustration. (NOTE: the game is great in all its modes, so if you still want to get into multiplayer, go ahead. After all, this is just MY OPINION, and if you want, you can ignore me. The game is fun even in multiplayer, but I hope you have a lot of patience and tolerance to learn, because if you get into it, you'll see a big difference between a “casual” player and a G80 who desperately needs to humiliate everything they see).

If you want an FPS campaign that makes you feel like an unstoppable action hero from start to finish, Titanfall 2 is the gold standard. It’s a highly mobile, incredibly fluid shooter where sliding and wall-running aren't just gimmicks—they are the core of how you survive. Gameplay & Mechanics Freedom of Motion: The movement system is flawless. Bounding off walls and sliding into engagements feels perfectly natural and makes complete sense within the universe. Gunplay: The weapon mechanics are snappy and designed to keep you moving. You're constantly encouraged to swap to whatever guns you find on the ground to keep the momentum going. The Titans: The power fantasy here is real. The moment you strap into your massive Titan, the dynamic shifts completely, and normal foot soldiers suddenly feel like mere mosquitoes against your hull. Level Design: The game constantly throws unique mechanics at you depending on the level, keeping the gameplay loop fresh without ever overstaying its welcome. Story & Audio The Campaign: It took me about 6 hours on regular difficulty, which felt like the absolute perfect length. It delivers an engaging story with just the right amount of world-building without bogging down the pacing. Immersion: The voice acting and music are both top-tier. They perfectly complement the action and never once pulled me out of the experience. Performance Visuals & Polish: The game looked and played great. Even years after its release, the art direction and smooth performance hold up incredibly well. Final Thoughts This is a masterclass in how to build a tight, no-filler single-player FPS. Whether you are zipping around as a pilot or stomping through maps in a mech, it’s a blast the entire way through. There is also still a multiplayer scene, that I was able to find games quickly at the time of the review.

What an amazing experience! Had a LOT of fun with this, and it is a near-perfect fps campaign. The best thing about Titanfall 2 is how it ENCOURAGES experimentation with gameplay styles. - You can only hold 2 guns at once, so players have a choice between swapping with any guns found on the floor or sticking to a preferred loadout for long periods of time. - In terms of movement??? You can WALLRUN, double jump, slide, perform super fun ONE-HIT melee attacks. - And as for the titans, there are like 9 different modes with different guns, abilities... REPLAYABILITITY IS OFF THE CHARTS IN THIS GAME. Now, every level in this game has some sort of interesting gimmick, whether it be one where you parkour on a mechanical factory, one where you solely play as a titan, one where you hack certain objects/platforms, OR A TIME TRAVEL FOCUSED LEVEL. Quite possibly the greatest level-design I have ever seen in an fps campaign. I am someone who came into this game KNOWING and ANTICIPATING the time travel level, but words cannot describe how immaculate it is to actually experience it---but I can try. As a new mechanic, the player is given a glove that with a singular button press, you swap timelines, and the best part?? THERE IS LIKE A 1 SECOND COOLDOWN. Imagine this, you're in the present and there's a malfunctioned door blocking the way, swap to the past and then the pathway is open, but there are like 50 guys ready to kill you. IMMEDIATELY swap back to the present, but then there are mutated animals ready to kill you as well. My favorite way to combat this? SWAP BACK TO THE PAST, kill like one or two guys while wall-running or sliding to prevent damage, SWAP BACK TO THE PRESENT and kill a couple animals, BACK AND FORTH SWAPPING, one-hit punch a guy, shotgun blast an animal---you turn into this invisible ninja. It is amazing ♥♥♥♥. Even the story, under its basic exterior being a good vs evil faction is a deeply emotional and powerful relationship between man and machine. You become attached to this one-dimensional robot throughout the short 5 hour adventure and it is so so good. At the end of the game, although I didn't get too attached to the story due to riveting gameplay, I couldn't believe how I was on the verge of tears as a result of these powerful characters. SUCH A GREAT GAME. Only nitpicks I can say are the noticeable sensory overload same as Doom 2016, and boss fights being too easy/short. They don't detract from the experience tho SOOO 9.7/10 YEAH.

Backlog: Game 5 Protocol 3: Protect the pilot I'm by no means a professional review writer, but, I have decided to write reviews on the games that I have finished from my backlog. Understand that reviews are subjective and experiences may differ from person to person. I may not have liked a game everyone else liked, or disliked a game everyone else disliked. I have not necessarily done everything there was/is to do in the game as I'm only playing games as a hobby. Keep that it mind as you read on. Art/Graphics - 8/10 I thought this games presentation was very good, the fluid movement of the titans, the movement of other people and the overall scenery was very nice to look at. The gun looks and animations were well done. Sound - 8/10 I thought the sounds and voices in this game were very nice. The voice of BT did a excellent job at playing a robot with a very literal interpretation of everything. BT: Pilot, exercise caution Cooper: You could say that again BT: Pilot, exercise caution - Cooper: Glad to have you in one piece BT BT: Over 25,000 actually The dialogue between the two really feels natural and flows very well. Soundtrack - 9/10 The soundtrack to this game was very good. There are a few pieces of it I have in my playlist to listen to in my own time. It does a good job at keeping you immersed in the game and helps build up some moments and enhances others. Story - 9/10 I thought the story was very good, although very short. A few hours and you're done with the entire thing. The majority of my hours in this game came from getting 100% of the achievements, namely the '...Becomes the master' achievement. I'm not that great when it comes to time based things, so it took me a few hours to get this achievement. Back to the story though, it was good enough to leave a lasting impression on me. From all the way at the start trying to get familiar with each other, to the end were protocols must be upheld. Gameplay - 9/10 I thought the gameplay for this game was very good, it felt very smooth and quick. The titans felt like they had some weight to them, the loadouts for the titans were varied enough to change how you approch things a little bit. Overall it was very nice to go running around at a blistering rate running circles around all the enemies. Overall - 9/10 I think this game is a very good game to experience. Though I don't think I could recommend getting it at full price. As even with going for all the achievements, I still only have about 16 or so hours at the time of this review. I'm not into the PvP multiplayer aspects of games so I couldn't say for sure if the online for this game is still there or not. If you are like me and don't play PvP stuff then I would just wait for this game to go on sale before you get it.

I'm sad I didn't finish this when I started it a long time ago. I will avoid spoilers in this review. As a first person movement shooter, this gives you sliding, wall riding, double jump, mech fighting, it's all really fun. This game looks and plays well, which would have been impressive alone. But they add more and more unique gameplay mechanics that I won't spoil. All I'll say is that this game does some unique things in very clever ways that no other game I've played has done. And it all works flawlessly and you could have a slightly different experience each time, but the wonderment of that first playthrough will probably be lost. Visually and graphically very good, interesting set pieces, stunning and smooth animations, and amusing moments I won't spoil. For some immediate negatives for me, the png images used for the comms link were a bit lame. I also don't think the bosses/enemies had much personality, some of the designs were a bit interesting but I couldn't tell you a single one of their names or stories. However, the gameplay is so damn good that I'm not really that concerned about it. The acting is pretty good overall in this. Really this game just shines in offering a unique and fun gameplay experience all the way through (only a little slow towards the start), I played this on Hard and it was perfect. The game also didn't seem to give me much ammo, and being a routine andy I'm glad for it because it forces you to pick up all sorts of guns around the map and just...try new things constantly. Not all of the guns are useful in all situations and some are a lot better than others but most of them are quite enjoyable. However, there's a lot of titan loadouts and boy they start dumping those on you before I really felt like I'd even mastered the first one. You can switch those whenever though but I'll need some more playthroughs to get them all down. As for the story, the universe dumps a lot of info on you and I couldn't really care to keep track of all the names and information, but the world was interesting and the moments between BT and Cooper kept me hooked. BT was a stunning performance, you actually end up caring about your titan by the end a lot. Happy to say no noticeable performance issues, with only minor bugs experienced, including the ability to get out of bounds without too much difficulty if you're trying to break the game as the movement mechanics give you the chance to do this so it's kind of expected if you're doing it on purpose. Titanfall 2 - Campaign Review 11 hours 50/50 achievements unlocked My 15th perfect game on Steam Completed February 2026 I beat this game last year on PS5, and originally finished it on Xbox One back in 2016. Now I’ve unlocked every achievement on Steam, Xbox, and the platinum on PlayStation. I’ve officially run out of ways to praise this campaign. Titanfall 2 is one of, if not the greatest, FPS campaigns ever made. Playing it in 4K at 120+ FPS on a 77” OLED, or even on a 34” ultrawide, is an absolute treat. It still looks fantastic and, more importantly, still feels incredible. The movement remains unmatched. Nothing since has replicated the flow of wall running, double jumping, sliding, and seamless transitions between pilot and Titan combat. Respawn absolutely nailed this campaign. It’s better than I remembered. The pacing is tight, the mechanics are layered but intuitive, and every mission feels deliberate. The platforming and traversal are still the best in the genre. I genuinely wish every shooter borrowed its movement system. I won’t describe specific story beats or level moments because that would be doing a disservice to anyone who hasn’t played it. This is a campaign you experience blind. It deserves that respect. I still can’t believe Titanfall 3 doesn’t exist. One of the best FPS campaigns of all time. Easy 10/10. BT-7274 is the GOAT.

Holy peak, this was absolute cinema! A Hollywood action blockbuster with satisfying FPS combat and a fun storyline that while not super complex, does a great job showing the fun dynamic and bond of Jack Cooper and his mech buddy BT. The combat is split into 2 different styles, on foot and in the mech. Playing as Jack was very fun. Sprinting, sliding, wall running, all the movement is incredibly smooth, probably the best I've played in an FPS game. Shooting feels very satisfying and there's a good amount of gun variety too. You feel agile, and powerful. There's also a cooldown that lets you turn invisible for a short amount of time, letting you sneak behind enemies or get a quick breather from overwhelming enemy backshots. There's even a decent variety for throwable items, grenades, electric stun grenades, Firestars, Gravity stars, and satchel charges. And on top of that, the melee one shots grunts, it feels so good. Playing as BT was also a peak power fantasy. 8 distinct classes (although I don't remember getting to play all of them in the campaign) that were all fun and felt powerful. Mech movement is definitely feels a bit slower, but thoroughly makes up for it with pure power. The fact that you can kill every human-sized enemy just by walking over them and crushing them with your mech feet is shows that much. I don't know what else to say other than it's just so peak The story is also good. It's not a super deep or complex storyline, but it doesn't need to be, and never tries to be. It's a story about a pilot and his mech, and their fun dynamic and bond, presented in bombastic set pieces, huge explosions, and tons of action. It's paced very well, nothing ever overstaying its welcome. Overall, peak fiction. I haven't played the multiplayer so I haven't commented on that (it's locked for some reason) this is just about the campaign. The game is absolutely a steal on sale for $4, and I'm sure the base $30 price tag would be worth it too, especially if you do plan on sinking time in multiplayer (which again, I haven't played, but I've heard is good). If you plan on getting the game just for the campaign though, it's probably best to wait for a sale though, as it's very short, like 5-6 hours long. I love you BT, I need you BT, Titanfall 3 when?

Most of my hours were on Origin, or I guess 'EA App' now. But, I bought the game again on Steam, since it was like $5 on sale, and I guess I played it a couple more times after beating it, and today I figured well hey, it's a pretty short game, and I haven't reviewed it, let's play Titanfall 2 yet again and sorta share my thoughts. Well, it's one of the best FPS games of the 2010s. It's an easy game to recommend. This is not a deep game, but it's a blissfully fun time all around, and since it's only about 4 hours long, you'll miss it when it is gone. And that's fine by me. This is in my opinion a pretty good example of 'wow cool robot' and kind of the upper ceiling of what that can be. A senseless, fun adventure that doesn't really do much of anything for you intellectually. It's an action movie type story, where you play a man allied with the Good Guys, Cooper, seemingly being mentored by a Pilot who thinks Cooper has potential. Pilots pilot Titans. Titans are seemingly rare on the Good Guys side as they are a 'militia' and the Bad Guys are a dominion with seemingly endless resources. There also seem to be mercenaries in this story on the side of the Bad Guys, which seems surprising given how relatively scarce they are. You can field, seemingly, like 100 men for 1 Titan. But anyway, all that's fine - it's not important. What is important is the attempt to make you care about a lifeless robot that follows you around named BT, and the reasonable success achieved there. Very quickly into the story, the ordinary soldier Cooper, aka you, manages to get a robot of his own, and if you're playing this game relatively normally you'll get lots of moments throughout the game to sort of chat with this robot and speak to it and form some kind of a bond, it's sort of like a robot dating sim, in the manly language of guns and shooting. So it's really nothing like a traditional relationship. It is great, though. The gameplay I think is the absolute star of the show here, however, this game just also happens to have pretty solid progression of events, a story that moves very quickly and consistently and is always moving and always driving you on to cool new things, new levels with new gimmicks and all sorts of stuff like that, it's just great. And the gimmicks are in the gameplay, which is stellar. While you are a man, Cooper, you are also a robot, whenever you choose to approach your robot and press E to Embark and Enter into your robot. Then, you become one, and you then are allowed to shoot and aim and punch and move with your robot, from a first-person perspective, and annihilate everything for as long as you want with no restrictions. Which is just great. Or, to put it in simpler terms - the game effortlessly, and fluidly allows you to play from the perspective of your regular man with Call of Duty guns, and the first person shooter experience that is piloting a huge robot, whenever you want! Which is, again, great. You, as Cooper have a wide selection of weapons and grenades with various attachments, you don't get to modify these, you just pick up stuff you loot off the dead and run around and Call of Duty enemies to death with such tools as 'Aim Down Sights' and 'Pulling the Trigger' - and this is great. The guns all feel fantastic to use. My only complaint is that the revolver shows up a bit too late, and it's hard to find ammo for it, so you only get to use it for about five minutes before the game is over. Oh well. Then as BT, your giant robot, you have about 8 different 'kits' you can put on and change from literally any time you want. You just press F1, and select a kit and go back to gameplay. There's no real problem here, because you already have infinite ammo in the robot anyway, mostly because you're not otherwise likely to find a stock of depleted uranium 20mm shells in convenient robot-sized magazines laying around and it probably wouldn't be too fun to have to hunt those anyway. And since you have infinite ammo in your giant robot, you can therefore swap between all your kits whenever you want without really upsetting the balance of the game. The kits are all pretty solid stuff. They all tend to have some kind of 'gameplan' and fight by executing that gameplan, so hopefully there's something for everyone, in terms of personal preference, and there's Tone if you just want to win I suppose. And later, Legion, which is also pretty good. Each loadout is a gun, and then a couple extra abilities you can press, and every Titan gets an ultimate of some sort you can do known as a Core. Cores usually let you do absurd amounts of damage very quickly. Everyone is a DPS in this game, and your DPS is raised significantly when you use a Core. So you've got your basic assault rifle type deal, then you have a missile launcher, a shotgun, a flame grenade launcher(?), and some other weapons. You kinda get the idea, you just get an assortment of different weapons. The abilities you get to go with these usually reflect on the weapon. If you have a missile launcher, you probably have a bunch of other stuff that shoots missiles, including a core that shoots ALL the missiles. It's that kind of game. If you have a shotgun, you probably also have a big mech sword, for close encounters. Interacting with the environment is a great time, because you get a dash as your big robot, so you can move around pretty quickly, and as a man, you can double-jump and run on walls and then jump off walls, to double jump onto another wall, and then run on that wall, recovering your double-jump all the while. So there's a lot of jumping and running and sliding and so on. It's a lot of fun, and getting good at it is genuinely pretty hard. Part of what makes it fun is, the game actually lets you get away with a lot of things, you preserve momentum for instance if you bunny hop off the ground quickly enough after landing. Going fast is really fun, and the limit is really just how good you can get at hopping around through levels. And that's just... great, really. Even if you're not good, the game will help you go fast from time to time, through setpieces and stuff. However, you're usually an active part in these which makes it that much more exciting. For the most part, you have full control over your movement, which makes these setpieces often a little more uncertain. But that's okay, the game is pretty aggressive with checkpoints and it loads your last save super fast, so even if you mess up you usually lose like no progress. It's really quite surprising that Titanfall 2 never saw any kind of endurance, and to this day nearly 10 years later, they still haven't announced some kind of a sequel. Most people tend to agree it is a spectacular singleplayer campaign, and the multiplayer was cool too, or what I played of it. This is pretty much a completely unreserved recommendation, I have nothing negative to say about Titanfall 2.

Protocol 3: Protect the Pilot Titanfall, the first game, was a weird one. It had a brilliant gameplay loop, an interesting world... but was (and still is) hindered by being exclusively a multiplayer title. The story wasn't half bad, but it's hard to take an interest when it's happening almost solely in the background whilst you're actively killing and getting killed in a fast-paced PvP shooter. Titanfall 2 fixes all that. It's got a brilliant campaign, set out with some very interesting set-pieces (just some random examples: a level where you get the ability to switch between past and present version of the location, a huge factory that builds... houses, or fighting on huge flying airships). And through the whole campaign (barring the initial intro mission) you get to use the expanded pilot mobility whilst on foot and the titan combat whilst in controlling the titan. By comparison CoD almost never does that - they introduce a gimmick, use it once, then discard it. The visuals, by today's standards, might be getting a wee bit dated, but they're ever so slightly stylized meaning it's really not bad on the eyes. And you get a really fun partner - your titan. Sure, he's got the classic trope of an "AI not getting human jokes and being way too literal", but it's all done in such an honest fashion you can't help but smile. And that's just the campaign. Once you're done there's the classic Titanfall multiplayer to explore which got streamlined quite a bit from TF1. Gone are the burn-cards and titan customizations - you get some fixed loadouts with minor perks. This may feel like a step back, but it actually means each titan feels different, plays different, and has a different role... whereas in TF1 all titans were "jacks of all trades" to a certain extent. Shields no longer recharge either, so while getting a titan is definitely a power boost it's almost sure to go down eventually, meaning players need to get comfortable both inside and outside of the metal shell. And if PvP isn't your thing there's also CO-OP PvE. It's got only a handful of maps, sadly, but on higher difficulties it's a really demanding mode, requiring players cooperate and play very well. In short - get it. I don't care if you get it at the EA store or here on Steam. Just get it. Play the campaign and fall in love with BT. Then take to the PvP or co-op PvE. PS. Don't let my playtime fool you. I've bought it way back when on the EA store. There's been a very nice sale on Steam with some goodies I didn't yet have, so I got it here as well (and since the accounts can be linked I now have extra stuff on my account for a fraction of the price). EDIT: After reading my own review I realised I wrote it whilst having a bit rose-tinted glasses. I thought it would be fair to list some of the negatives of the title as well, for any potential newcomers. - the game requires the EA launcher - there are a few long-lasting bugs from the campaign - nothing major, but they STILL exist to this day - multiplayer is NOT balanced; or rather, it's balanced around casual gaming, and not sweaty pro players... be weary of pros, for they will easily dominate (thankfully they tend to handicap themselves and stick to less desirable, high-skill weapons) - given the title is quite old multiplayer is fairly empty, and and the queue times can be quite long

This game is a masterpiece. Here's my personal list of what makes it so great: -One of, if not the most in-depth movement systems you'll ever see. Pilot jumpkit movement combined with source engine airstrafing makes for a ridiculously fun combination, and the skill ceiling is basically nonexistent with how much tech you could possibly learn. Coming from someone who has a fair bit of experience in all sorts of parkour-y and other movement-y games, this is THE best movement shooter on the market. Highly recommend watching a few video essays on TF2 speedrunning if you're interested. -A frankly underrated system of balance between the multiplayer titan classes. Every titan has a unique balance of strengths and weakness, situations they excel in and ones where they fall short. Learning how to effectively use each titan's kit and learning all the matchups between titans is tons of fun. -A shockingly compelling campaign that I've replayed easily dozens of times. Even if you're completely uninterested in the multiplayer aspect of TF2, playing through the campaign is well worth your money. I'm not about to say it's the most emotionally compelling story you'll every experience, because it's not, but it's quite thorough and a damn lot of fun. BT is best character. -A huge arsenal of weapons, ordinance, and tacticals to choose from that let you play in all sorts of creative ways. There's obvious metas (Grapple + CAR, I'm looking at you), but pretty much every loadout you can cobble together is viable if you know what you're doing. One of my favorite weapons, the Mozambique, is generally regarded as a meme weapon (which it kind of is), but I'm still able to regularly perform well with it. -Immaculate vibes, and a great sense of scale. Never before or since playing this game have I seen another game demonstrate the feeling of piloting a giant robot quite so well. Not to mention, map design (in and out of multiplayer), the background art, the enemy designs, and everything else there is to look at are all phenomenally done. There looks to be some pretty neat lore, too, but I never really picked up on the specifics. -Best of all, a whole slew of interesting characters to meet in the MP lobbies. If you go five matches without seeing some weird sh*t in the network chat or somebody completely losing it in in-game chat, I'd be shocked. Believe it or not, I love this. The people who play this game are endlessly entertaining.

I have several hundred hours on console, and still find myself coming back to this game even years later. Many have attested to the great singleplayer campaign and the absolutely amazing movement mechanics, so I won't detail them here. But I will say that the game as a whole is one that respects its players. It's a complete package with actual "micro"-transactions (while they do have a chance to give double xp tokens after a match, it applies to *everyone* on your team, not just those who bought the skin), and even those are completely unnecessary due to the massive amount of free unlockable cosmetics. The progression system is great, as you repeatedly unlock things every time you get enough xp to regenerate, unlocking more cosmetics in the process. Note that you can permanently unlock everything after gaining enough in-game (not paid) currency. And besides all that, the gameplay is really fun, action-packed, and varied in style depending on gamemode and your loadout. There's even a 4-player co-op defense type gamemode which is completely underrated for how unique, challenging (at higher difficulties), and enjoyable it is thanks to unlockable titan-specific upgrade paths that can massively boost the power of your titans or in some cases even add new functionality. And while now match queue times can be a bit long, it's still well worth it and now you can easily mod it to play on custom servers with new cosmetics, mechanics, etc, or just use modded cosmetics in the base game with proper matchmaking via Vanilla+ I could continue on, but basically what I'm trying to say is this game is a masterpiece, especially at sale price, If you like FPS games, even in passing, TF|2 is 100% worth a buy.

Titanfall 2 is honestly one of those rare games that flows from start to finish without ever getting boring. The level design is incredibly well thought out, and the gameplay never feels repetitive. One of its biggest strengths is that there are barely any cutscenes, so nothing really interrupts your gameplay. The story is told while you play, which keeps you fully immersed. The mission where you can jump back and forth through time is especially amazing. That level alone is worth playing the game for. The graphics are still rock solid even today; despite its age, it still looks better than many newer games. The multiplayer is surprisingly still active and a lot of fun. Movement mechanics, wall-running, calling in Titans — everything still feels unique and satisfying. The weapons feel great too, especially the one you get at the end, which I really liked. The story is also much better than expected. You actually connect with the characters, and I don’t remember getting bored for even a moment. It also doesn’t drag on unnecessarily; it ends at just the right length. When it’s over, you’re left thinking, “I’m really glad I played this.” I used to be sad that I never played the first game, but after checking and seeing it was basically multiplayer-only, I didn’t feel so bad. Still, it would be amazing if a third game came out — Apex gives little flashes of what that could look like. Final verdict: Definitely play it. If you like FPS games you’ll love it, and even if you don’t, this might change your mind.

[h1]A Good Campaign That Never Quite Becomes a Great Shooter[/h1] The campaign is short, and once you get acquainted with the movement systems for both the pilot and the Titan (which takes a few missions), it becomes a good experience. But for me, it never reached the highs of a truly great shooter. However, after just finishing COD & Battlefield(Both newer and world war shooters), it didn't have that punch, that oomph feel that comes from a great shooter. These games differ in setting and pacing, but they share one thing Titanfall 2 lacks for me: gunplay and difficulty that consistently reward positioning, timing, and player intent. Arcade shooters have a place, but when the game’s framing, tone, and presentation suggest a grounded, realistic experience, the underlying arcade design clashes with the expectations it sets. [h2]Flaws:[/h2] [olist] [*][b]Guns:[/b] I didn't like how a lot of guns felt so I mostly stuck with a few "realistic" guns throughout. The large sniper, the guns that sound and shoot like guns and what not. They tried to mix and match things up and some might like that, I didn't. [*][b]Difficulty:[/b] The difficulty in other great shooters comes from positioning and shooting. Here the enemy AI even on hard just stays in the open waiting for you to shoot and to increase difficulty, enemy spawns are increased, explosive pressure rather than smarter positioning or flanking behavior. When I died here, it rarely felt like it was justified and conversely when I did kill a Titan, I didn't feel like I did something great. [*][b]Realistic Framing vs. Arcade Feel:[/b] Everything the game shows makes you feel you are going to play a realistic shooter with some futuristic weapons but very quickly it turns into an arcade shooter. The above points add to it. [/olist] [b]Final thoughts[/b]: I can see why people love the campaign and this game. The movement system, level variety, and late-game Titan sections are genuinely fun, which is why I still recommend the campaign. However, the short length, uneven Titan integration, tone mismatch and difficulty design kept it from being the shooter game I loved to play. It's a good game, just not a great one. [h1]Expectations to set[/h1] [olist] [*][b]Multiplayer is effectively inactive[/b] Servers are locked. You can't play Multiplayer. Thanks EA. [*][b]Campaign is short[/b]. It's like 6 hours on hard difficulty and lower on other difficulty. I took my time with it still couldn't cross 6 hours. It might have been fine but the lack of Titan parts was really a let down as it was only into the end game that the Titan part of the game really started to show its colors. [*][b]The first cutscene set the wrong expectation for me for the Mech/Titans[/b] Based on that I expected the Mech/Titan to be as fast and fluid as the character or even what was shown in the first cutscene when playing the game. Once I got over the fact that those expectations were wrong after a lot of playthrough, I was fine with it. Then 3/4th through the game I finally got the play the Titan properly and that was when the Titan started to click and I had a bunch of fun. [*][b]Play on one higher difficulty than what you normally play on[/b] The enemy AI isn't really smart even on Hard so it's really recommended you increase your difficulty by one when going into this. [/olist] [h1]Price Recommendation[/h1] Short Campaign and dead multiplayer means it's best experienced during huge sales (80-90% off) which it goes on regularly.

It should always be noted that I am a person who likes flawed games. Sometimes a game doesn’t need to be amazing to be a good game. Either by the game looking pretty, the mix of insane challenge and freedom, how incredibly fun it is to just play it, or if the Dev is a cool person. I say this because when I find a game that is flawless, with everything it is doing, and how impressive it is in… NOW… It could be a game that leaves me shocked in the best way ever… TitanFall2 is this exact game… in every way… I don’t care how you and/or I feel about EA, Respawn, or Apex Cheeked up Legends, NOTHING was gonna stop this game from being good. Now granted, I didn’t really play this for the Multiplayer, I played a little bit and I kinda suck. But that is less of a critique and more of a skill issue. Besides, I always view the Singleplayer to be 10% more important than the Multiplayer: because where the Multiplayer once lived and then will go on to quietly die, the Singleplayer is… ETERNAL… This is to say that the Campaign is SO GOOD, that like… It makes me wish that there was more with how good it was… ]: Cooper Controls fantastically, FPS x Platforming has always been a genre that I’ve wanted to explore. And this game has probably been the best example of mixing both seamless, probably one of the best First Person Shooter games I have ever played. And that Extends to the Titans (mostly BT-7274). Because even though the game expects you to attack from a safe distance and wants you to use your abilities very strategically ; The game doesn’t mind if you want to get close to the enemy and just punch the ♥♥♥♥ out of the enemy with the base move set that you start with. Because with how the game is built, the game doesn’t mind if as Cooper: you slow down and take the time to kill every enemy in your path, or Speed past like Sonic the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Hedgehog. The story is simple, the average sci-fi military shoot game, and that’s all this game needed really. But even though I don’t care about 99% of the characters in this game, the absolute BROMANS between Jack Cooper and BT-7274 is easily one of the very best of this game’s story. No ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in game politics, nor an overly complex Villain that nobody will remember, what this game has is 2 bros driving and dashing to their heart content, and will help each other out in order to save for what they both love for… And trust me, I felt something after BT-7274 processed to take on the ultimate sacrifice… I am not sad about it, what do you mean I am crying??... ;-; Cons: This game has very little issues, practically none. In fact, I don’t remember a SINGLE TIME that I’ve gotten angry at the game. Never once did I have a moment that I’ve raged or was like: “That is complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥…” Because this game Passed great, ran Fantastically on my PC, and was just flat out an Enjoyable experience all away through. So even though I have my fair share of Cons here, they really don’t make a difference on how Good this game is: - The slide is a little strange… in the way it doesn't quite work as a way to start off momentum. And also you kinda have to slow down in order to shoot. Nether of these are things that effected the way I played, but it did slip me up a few times when starting - This is an EA Game… So I had to make an EA account to just play this... I understand why, but It is kinda annoying to have to sign up for an account to just play one game... - But the WORST part of the game was at the end… Right after beating Slone, the hardest boss, I was expecting to then after Kuben Blisk. After all, the whole level was built up to being allowed to fight him. But after he lays the “Apex” card on you… The game… Ends… It couldn’t end like this, there is so much that was left unresolved, I NEEDED MORE!!! ;-; Closing Statement: Ultimately if EA never ends up release Titanfall3, or if they do and it flops, well… I wont be to mad about it… This game is one of the best games I have ever played, and when I though that there was a point where it will chill out and calm down with it’s coolness, It looks at the player and says, “♥♥♥♥ YOU, TIMETRAVEL THAT WORKS REALLY GOOD SOMEHOW!!” The only thing I wish this game had, was an option to have sex with your beefy as robot boyfrie- 10/10 Game “Better than Remember, Still bad End…” - FUNKe
