There's a lot with this game so I'm just gonna to a pros and cons list: Pros: - As of 2025 standards, the game is visually stunning. - Weekly/Monthly challenges so there's reason to come back in check in. - Some of these cars are FUN to drive. Controller or wheel some of these cars are just a blast to use. - Again as of 2025 standards, the system requirements are pretty broad so you can kind of play this game on anything. - Online is a blast! Even if it's just bumming around the overworld or playing some random races against bots with your friend the game is an easy comfort game to play (This goes for all Forza Horizon games that still have online servers). - Some might see this as a con, but the game is very arcade'y for racing game standards. I love this! let me pull off some insane stunts! It's much more friendly for a casual audience that just wants a good time with no headaches. Cons: - It's nice that there's a butt ton of cars... But like 40% of them feel like hot garbage to control, and most people don't wanna spend hours to make their car feel good to drive in. - Car availability is HORRIFIC!!! You want a certain car that's not in the autoshow? Pray it's in the auction house and have an extra 20mil credits ready to hopefully buy it out before someone else does. You can literally game the system and earn credits faster by scalping and reselling cars in the auction house compared to actually playing the game. - (This is a Steam specific issue) If you buy Horizon off steam and want to play it on your Xbox you have to buy the game again on the Xbox storefront. It's an "Xbox play anywhere" title so it should support this, but this is a totally separate issue that's from my understanding on Steam's end and not Microsoft's. - DLC. I get the game has expansions, but some of the "car packs" offered are just a waste of money. - Bots have overran the leaderboards. So don't expect a top 10% in anything Long story short: This is a Horizon title, so the game's a really fun casual experience to play solo or with friends. If you're looking for a more realistic racing sim experience, this game ain't it (Assetto Corsa is more what you're looking for). 8.9/10 IMPORTANT: For god's sake if you want to play this game on both Xbox and PC buy it off the Microsoft Store!!! If you buy the game off the Microsoft Store you will only need to buy the game once to play on either device. IF YOU BUY THE GAME OFF STEAM YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO PLAY IT ON XBOX, IT WILL BE PC ONLY AND YOU WILL NEED TO PURCHASE THE GAME AGAIN TO PLAY ON XBOX.

I recommend this game, but it has some significant drawbacks. Overall I give it a 7/10 and if you're looking for a casual, open world racing game with a TON of cars and lots of stuff to do, then it's pretty good. Positives- 1. There's a massive amount of cars of all types from many different car companies. There's over 800 cars in the game which is almost an overwhelming amount. They have every major brand and a lot of obscure ones too. There's cars from almost every era including 1920s racers but it mostly focuses on modern stuff. 2. The open world is very well designed and there's TONs to do and explore. There's desert dunes, jungle waterfalls, a snow topped volcano and everything in-between. They did a great job on the level design and the whole place is filled with fun stuff to do. 3. There's a wide variety of racing types and tracks. There's rally, cross country, midnight run style street races, circuit races, drag racing and tons more. There is also a track designer that is very flexible and you can make your own tracks and share them and race with friends. You won't run out of tracks. 4. Car customization is excellent. You can paint your car how you like or use other peoples paint jobs and tuning setups. Really nice to be able to paint your car how you like. 5. You can tune the difficulty of AI racers to how you like. Negatives- 1. The competitive multiplayer is ABSOLUTE TRASH. Do not buy this game for the online racing aspect, unless you're going to play with friends. Once you get to a certain point in the game, you will need to do a weekly "coop" race with other online players VS. the hardest AI drivers in a best of 3 battle. Unfortunately, over half the time your idiot teammates will spend most of their time and effort ramming and wrecking you and other players instead of beating the AI team, causing the whole team to waste 20 minutes and get nothing. In any type of online racing, you will be mercilessly rammed by online jerks and there is ZERO penalty for them to do so. There's no damage model and no points penalty for ramming or forcing other players off the road to miss checkpoints or hit stuff. The online racing is a complete dumpster fire full of jerks who WILL ram and wreck you constantly. 2. The developer is incredibly greedy. Despite launching a 100$ Premium edition, they still released a bunch of DLC cars (that you totally don't need) that were not included in the purchase. To make things even worse, these extra car packs NEVER go on sale (at the time of this writing). The greedy developers also stopped releasing any NEW content early in 2025, despite the fact that FH6 will not be out for years. So everything you're buying will just be recycled events and there will never be any new cars. Expect this game to get delisted from steam in a few years like they did with FH4 because they're literally too cheap to renew the car licensing rights. 3. The game has total Xbox-ification. You will need to make an xbox live gaming account and will be forced to use this awful system to find your friends, etc. despite this being on Steam. 4. There is no real car damage in the game. Your million dollar supercar can ram through metal guardrails, stone walls, fences or even small trees with absolute ease! The worst damage your car will suffer is a cracked windshield, which is annoying if you play in first person. Your car can look a bit scuffed up, lose a spoiler or side mirrors but the damage never affects performance, which is one reason people ram into each other so much. This is NOT a realistic racer. The only stuff that will really stop your car is a large tree, massive boulder or a building. There's also no tire wear or refueling. 5. You always start near the back of the field in ANY race. There is no qualifying or practice options, you just go in cold with no warmup laps or anything to get to know the car. There's so many cars that you're constantly changing so you don't really get used to racing with one car for long periods of time. 6. The "plot" is just junk. They try to make a plot around you being the best driver in the world and it's just paper thin. They also try and fail horribly to incorporate Mexican culture and history into racing. One example of this is there is an entire storyline about Mexican Wrestling and cars, and yes, this plot is absolutely as horrendous as you'd expect. Forza Horizon 4 had Top Gear as the guests for one plot series and it was good and funny. This game has the insufferable goons from Donut Media cleverly mispronouncing words like horsepower. The plot is luckily skippable and you don't have to play much of it to unlock the whole game. 7. This is not a SIM by any means. Besides the aforementioned lack of damage, tire wear, or fueling, I would say the physics aren't 100% accurate. Rain seems to affect traction very little and there is literally not a single pothole or manhole cover in the ENTIRE country of Mexico! Amazing! There's no bumps in the road or even a speedbump. Don't expect extreme realism here, it's more a game you can play with a controller than requiring a wheel. This is more of a casual, have some beers and race around type game. 8. The hotwheels expansion isn't that great. It turns out that racing around narrow plastic orange lanes at super high speeds gets old after a few hours. 9. The game throws so many cars at you early in the game that you never really establish a bond or an affinity for many cars. It certainly doesn't have a career mode or anything. You'll just get a ton of fast cars right away. 10. Every global leader board for fastest times are completely filled with hackers and totally impossible times and the developers refuse to fix them or delete them. So with all these negatives, why do I give this game a 7/10? Well, it's super fun for what it does. It's a casual open world racing game where you can do what you want and collect and customize over 800 cars, which is pretty badass! The open worlds are huge, full of different terrain, they did a fantastic job with the level design. Just know that this is a more casual racer, that the developers are super greedy and that the online mode with random people is absolute trash due to ramming. If you love cars and just messing around driving, you can easily have 200+ hours of enjoyment out of this game. You can also really make the game your own with a custom dressed up character, totally custom paint and a full, powerful map editor to make your own tracks and share them. Just don't expect sim level physics, any kind of damage or the plot to be any good! If you've got friends to play with instead of randoms, the online component gets better as well. Also, since this game is getting "old" now and will likely get some pretty good Steam discounts, I highly recommend the Complete Edition since you'll get double the VIP points (used for getting weekly rare cars) and comes with both expansion packs which add large areas to the game. Hope this helps and watch out for those rammers!

how to make delicious Butter Chicken. ----------------------------------------------------------- Ingredients for 4 servings, 2 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (910 g), cubed salt, to taste pepper, to taste 2 teaspoons chili powder, divided ½ teaspoon turmeric 6 tablespoons butter, divided 1 ½ cups yellow onion (225 g), diced 3 teaspoons garam masala 1 teaspoon cumin 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper 1 tablespoon ginger, grated 3 cloves garlic, minced 1 cinnamon, 3 inch (8 cm) stick 14 oz tomato sauce (395 g) 1 cup water (240 mL) 1 cup heavy cream (240 mL) rice, for serving fresh cilantro, chopped for garnish. Preparation In a large bowl, season the chicken breast with salt, pepper, 1 teaspoon of chili powder, and the teaspoon of turmeric. Let sit for 15 minutes to marinate. Melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken, then remove from the pot. Melt another 2 tablespoons of butter in the pot, then add the onion, garam masala, remaining teaspoon of chili powder, the cumin, ginger, garlic, cayenne, cinnamon, salt and pepper. Cook until fragrant. Add the tomato sauce and bring to a simmer. Add the water and cream and return to a simmer. Return the chicken to the pot, cover, and simmer for another 10-15 minutes. Stir in the last 2 tablespoons of butter and season with more salt and pepper to taste. Serve the chicken over rice and garnish with cilantro. Enjoy!

There’s an endless supply of missions, seasonal events, unique cars, and just an insane overall vehicle roster. And the best part? You can play it however you want: run missions, ignore them completely, just cruise across the massive open world, drift, race on tracks, or dive into user-created maps. It’s pure freedom. Both DLCs – Hot Wheels and Rally Adventure – are absolutely worth it, each adding a brand-new map. They’re not as big as the main one, of course, but they’re packed with detail and full of fun. Overall 10/10. One of the best games I’ve ever played, and a masterpiece of the genre.

I can recommend this game ONLY if you seek something where you can drive cars around and nothing else. This aspect could give you a dozen or so hours after which you will get bored and put the game on a shelf (if you can endure everything else about the game). Yes, it is extremely well optimized, has loads of cars and has great visuals. However. There is no progression. The second you launch the game, you are awarded with gazillion of hypercars, currency and dozens of gambling spins. Besides driving the cars the game will, basically, play itself. You do not start in some rusty hatchback that your dad left you and progress from the bottom. You do not need to strive to do races to get some shiny supercar you always wanted. You do not have an opponent you really want to beat as every other driver is a faceless shadow without personality, or a face and personality so horrible you wish they didnt have either. You do not feel like your reputation grows, like you overcome something. There is no stroy. There is no decision making. There is no ending because you already start with everything bending to your will. Every event you do is meaningless - you DO NOT need to adapt or overcome the challenges to progress. You cannot lose, often even if you finish 10th, because the game doesn't want you to feel sad. Yes, the game literally treats you like a social media addicted basement dweller that gets offended from a single word. Or a journalist. Don't know which is worse. A race? You can drive whatever the hell you want and upgrade your car however you like, your opponents will just adjust to whatever you roll to the starting grid. A time trial? Just drive through the flat desert in your koenigsegg without even thinking about using the road (because of course your hypercar can drive on sand and dirt like a rally car) and finish minutes ahead of the "best" score. High score challenge? Just do whatever, no need to try chaining drifts into jumps and precise traffic avoidane - I am serious - game rewards you with points for EVERY action you make, just dont crash too hard. Map design is atrocious, as beside the edges of the map (20% of the whole thing) where there are actually some obstacles or problematic terrain you might need to cope with, the rest is a flat, boring, uninspired desert. And why is it there, you ask? Because devs thought that a car battle royale would be a good idea. It wasn't. Like I said earlier, there is no story. But what about the dialogue? Yes there are plenty of voice acted lines. You would wish they weren't the second you hear a single one. Everyone is so over the top, cheesy, and cringy while doing their voice over for poorly written dialogue that the game actually becomes a better experience with voices turned off completely. Music choice is bland and just barely above the atrocious taste of whoever picked music for recent NFS games. Yes they also mute words like "die" if they appear in lyrics. AI will either be a grandma with asthma or a volkswagen beetle that would blitz past you with 30km/h speed advantage despite you driving a bugatti at its top speed. If you played other FH games the "big events" the game throws at you do not have that "wow" factor you got after racing a plane for the first time, or trying to outplace some dirt bikers in a forest. It was all done before, and there is nothing in them besides the heavily scripted "tense" moments sprinkled here and there. Overall, and I'm completely serious here, FH games have so much untapped potential to become best in genre, but the developers simply refuse it in favour of appealing to kiddies who are satisfied from just seeing shiny cars go fast. I really, really hope (but have zero realistic expectations if we look at how they addressed these problems before - they didn't) that the next franchise entry would have a proper career mode with an actual engaging story and progression. That these stupid gambling wheelspins would be locked until you complete it. That the map and physics would be designed in a way so you can't cut a corner of a well-paved road through some mud while being in a lamborghini and gain time. That the dialogues would be written by an actual writer and not some blue haired middle aged woman from their HR department. That the purchases you make would have importance and require weighing pros and cons of different cars before you buy one. That the devs would actually take time and handcraft races with proper limitations to force players to interact with different car classes and mechanics - force them to buy some japanese sportscar to attend a championship, force them to upgrade their car to gain an advantage, force them to save money to get that hypercar for the final part of the game. Maybe also make purchase of housing mandatory if palyers want a bigger garage? At least up until the story is over and they can do whatever? Please? It's such a shame that's this franchise is [i]still[/i] somehow the best option racing genre has to offer. [spoiler]If only Test Drive Unlimited 3 didn't fumble the bag so hard that it lost all of its individuality and turned into another "almost FH" clone[/spoiler]

Forza Horizon 2, 3, and 4, were all way better in my opinion. This game suffers from extremely generous progression (e.g. allowing you to get multiple supercars and hypercars within the first few hours of playing) which feels nice at first but quickly discards the necessity of ever using the majority of your cars. The roads feel very easy to drive on; there's very few hairpins or chicanes/esses and the roads being wide and generous exacerbate the design philosophy of cars going fast rather than drivers. It makes the sense of speed in this game feel slow, with high centre-of-gravity cars remaining extremely planted and having a large margin for error in terms of steering angle even at 300-350km/h. The AI also feels very strange with lower difficulty AI being easily overtaken with trail braking and switchbacks and then suddenly jumping in difficulty to where AI drivatar trucks can take hard turns better than track-focused cars like Porsches. I understand the game is arcade-y but weight transfer isn't really a worry in that regard for cornering, and cars with the best specs seem to dominate rather than having cars play into specific strengths (i.e. Porsches best at cornering and Corvettes for off-the-line power). Lastly, many of the iconic cars (NSX-R, SVJ, GT3RS, 720s, F90 CS) are either only acquired through time-limited events (FOMO) or have incredibly high auction prices, and there's nothing to differentiate them spec-wise other than their demand as there's no reason to purchase one considering you're essentially guaranteed to have an S2 or X level car within the first 10ish hours anyway. This game is serviceable in my opinion as an arcade open-world driving game but if you're looking for something more focused in terms of the actual driving experience, I'd recommend Assetto Corsa instead.

[b]Overall, a good Forza Horizon game. Not without flaws, though.[/b] My second Forza Horizon game that I played. Overall, I enjoyed this game, mainly from the gameplay aspect. It's better than FH4, gameplay-wise. Starting from the improved physics, better server connection (much faster), great car sounds (compared to FH4's, which are horrendous), and more things to do (EventLab is a great addition to the franchise). Of course, despite these improvements, this game is not without flaws. First, the most obvious one: story. Man, the story feels like it's catered towards three-year-olds. Even then three-year-olds would most likely hate it. Second, the soundtrack. Don't get me wrong, they're nice to listen to. But it's obviously not curated. The songs sometimes feel like they're chosen because they're popular, not because they fit the festival vibe/theme. Also, the censorship is actually even worse than in FH4, and I hate that. Third, the map. Stupid decision to cater it to The Eliminator. A mode that has been abandoned since release. The result? Boring map. Yes, there's a lot of stuff here and there, but the middle of the map is just too empty. You obviously can still put stuff there. Major miss since Mexico still has more to offer. The rest are minor issues, like the quirky server (convoy missing randomly, not all players visible), some accolades not working (bugged), and the lack of progression (can make the game feels boring faster). I hope FH6 doesn't have the flaws that FH5 has. Better story (age rating shouldn't influence writing like in FH5), better server (FH4 server with FH5 connectivity speed), better map (catered towards car culture, preferably), better soundtrack (curate it and don't censor it to kingdom come (GT7 doesn't censor their soundtrack despite having the same age rating as FH5. Hell, even FH3 didn't censor its soundtrack with the same freaking age rating.), and some other improvements, minor or major. Also, improve the customization (improve or remove those garbage-looking Forza Aero).

EDIT: I'm quite thankful that Steam allows reviews to be edited. For the general review of the content itself, below, all still applies. For the edit, this is all technically related, and how Xbox and Microsoft continue to fail us. Crashes. They're starting to happen. I just had a 2hr play session with 2 crashes. Not necessarily a big deal but I never had crashes before recently. Sign in bug: There is a bug where it tells you you have to sign in. The idiotic passkey they force you to scan via QR code gets stuck in a loop and doesn't work ORRRRRR it gets stuck in a loop telling you to sign in while not presenting you the ability to sign in. The fact that I have to sign in to a game that is not solely multiplayer online is already questionable, but then for signin to have difficulties itself is intolerable and inexcusable. The Forza support feels like an afterthought with canned methods to try to fix the issue, that don't work. So instead the community has to pick up the slack where they fail us. The workaround that worked for me was to go into credential manager and delete all xbox related credentials, then go into the C drive, find the FH5 folder and delete it. THEN you can sign in. I hadn't been able to play my game for months until I found that fix, and every few days I have to do it again. Deplorable. Visual bugs. The latest Windows update introduced a visual bug in the form of two large rectangular black shadows on the road. It is as yet unfixed. Conclusion: I adore this franchise. I have loved every single entry and this game is no exception. But I am beyond furious at Microsoft and Xbox's expert ability to fail their customers in the most grand way possible. A game that worked PERFECTLY since launch now has issues that they seem uninterested in addressing, and if they ARE, they feel no need to communicate such. It makes one wonder if they'll get their act together before Forza Horizon 6 launches, since they'll want it to sell. One thing is for certain; they are currently presenting an air of indifference that is disappointing and that I personally resent. Bear these issues in mind before buying this game. I was ecstatic about rumblings of FH6 back before I started having these issues, and now that excitement is sullied by this nonsense. Here's hoping against hope that someone over there actually cares to fix this game. Having never had an Xbox before the Series X (which I subsequently sold to finance my GPU on my first (and current) PC a couple years ago, The Forza Horizon series was always one I'd wanted to play. Fortunately I was able to track down the disks for the first 3 before I sold them and my console. I worked my way through all the games while on Xbox and all of them were fantastic. Knowing they discontinue entries after a time I immediately re-purchased FH4 and 5 on PC. One of the most standout things about FH5 is its return to having something of a story! Although I loved every game, the first entry always held a special place because it had a little story to it. FH5 returned to form with that, and also featured some cameos that got me in the feelings. lol. It would not have hit me the same way if I'd missed out on the previous games. It's unfortunate many won't have that same experience. I'm playing on an RTX 4080 Super/Ryzen 7800X3D. The game runs flawlessly at 4k maxed settings. Without DLSS my framerate is in the triple digits. With DLSS (no framegen) the game maxes out my OLED TV at 144fps. The raytracing is FANTASTIC, as is the sound. TL;DR Buy if you like sandbox games and a lot of stuff in a game overall, if you hate grinding, or if you want a more realistic racing game than other arcade ones. Better don't buy for competitive multiplayer racing. Forza Horizon is not your typical arcade racing franchise. [b]It's more realistic[/b] with all its pros and cons. You'll find yourself countersteering to avoid unwanted drifting, managing the throttle, finding best parts combinations for your playstyle and the event etc. You will not drift every corner and once you mess one up, the consequences will be immediately noticeable (especially in multiplayer). However you can adjust the difficulty pretty thoroughly, as well as add several assists. With the right adjustment the game can be accessible even for pretty young and inexperienced players. Possibly the biggest advantage of the Horizon franchise has always been the [b]enormous car list[/b] and this title is no exception. With all DLCs and rare cars it goes beyond 800 vehicles (there are a few semi trucks lol), all with unique handling and capabilities. Speaking of cars, they are extremely easy to obtain. This is a part of another unique (and subjective) thing about the franchise - [b]extremely fast progression[/b]. You can easily get around 3 cars per hour (not even counting rewards from weekly events), as well as other rewards such as clothes and money (which you can use to buy even more cars). Btw money is usually not a problem at all (unless you're trying to buy all the most expensive cars) so you will never find yourself grinding for upgrades (which are all purchaseable with in game currency; no levels or microtransactions there), unlike in most of the other games. The game [b]does not have a proper story[/b]. The "campaign" is basically just a long tutorial. After that you're free to do whatever you want. All features are unlocked. That brings us to another major difference of Forza Horizon compared to other franchises - [b]the game is a sandbox[/b]. This means you need to know how to entertain yourself and use the game's features for it. There are weekly challenges with rare rewards but that's basically it in terms of what the game "wants" you to do. Everything else is up to you, whether you like it or not. When it comes to competitive playstyle, the game offers quite a lot of options, and the leaderboards are extremely competitive. There are also less competitive gamemodes such as Playground Games (various arcade games), The Eliminator (battle royale) and Hide And Seek. However it's important to note that [b]the game is not built for competitive play. Factors such as FPS may affect the laptime and result in an unfair experience[/b]. There are also cheaters but you can just report and ignore those. [b]Performance and optimization are great[/b], just like in FH4. The game works on any decently modern hardware. You don't need a high end PC even for ultra settings. The game features some microtransactions but the only thing you can get from them is common cars which you can also get for in game currency. You can't even get rare cars for real money. That is really good. I won't even highlight this section. When it comes to FH5 specifically, there are some differences from the previous games. Most noticeably, [b]car handling was simplified[/b] on keyboard and controller, offroading was simplified overall, and wheel support was greatly improved. So if you want a more hardcore experience on anything except for steering wheel, I'd suggest FH4 or FH3. Trust me, it can get very intense there, especially offroad. Also there are more arcade gamemodes in FH5 which have already been mentioned above. In terms of [b]issues[/b], the most noticeable one is [b]meta gaming[/b]. It means that some cars have an unfair advantage in their respective use cases. This can make the experience repetitive if you're trying to be very competitive. Similarly to that there is [b]ramming[/b] - unsportsmanlike behavior of others players who try to ram you off the road, resulting in you losing the race. The issue is really common and needs to be aknowledged at all times during multiplayer sessions (aka get ready to get rammed and use defensive manuevers in any suspicious situation). Also note that your teammates can ram too (very frustrating ik). So in conclusion, the game features extremely fast progression and a lot of features but does not force the player to do anything specific. This can be good or bad depending on your preference. I personally love that. Also the game is far from the best in terms of competitive play so do not buy it just for that.

As a car guy, or a car enthusiast, Forza Horizon 5 provides a tonne of touches into the car details. From the stunning graphics that bring each vehicle to life to the intricate sound design that captures the roar of the engines, every aspect has been meticulously crafted. This attention to detail not only enhances the driving experience but also immerses players in a vibrant automotive world. What makes this game feel different from any other racing series? Is its philosophy. Where Need for Speed thrives on underground street racing and title challenges, Forza Horizon embraces the celebration of car culture itself. It’s not only about racing; it’s about exploration, creativity, and community. The open-world setting in Mexico is expansive and diverse, offering everything from deserts and rainforests to bustling towns and ancient ruins. Players are encouraged to drive not just to compete, but to discover, photograph, and enjoy the beauty of the world. Beyond traditional racing, the Horizon Festival format allows for casual cruising, stunt challenges, showcase events, and even player-created content, making the experience broader than a simple competition. With an unmatched car roster, seamless multiplayer integration, and constant seasonal updates, Forza Horizon 5 stands as both a tribute to automotive passion and a playground for anyone who simply loves the joy of driving. Verdict: More than a racing game, Forza Horizon 5 is a living celebration of car culture — blending authenticity, freedom, and spectacle in ways no other franchise does.

This is the best racing game out there. Just based on technical issues, I can safely not recommend you buy it though. This might seem odd, but hear me out: The game constantly crashes. But it saves everything up to the crash and it crashes either before the race begins or after it ends. Saving your progress along the way. So crashing isn't as frustrating, but you also cannot skip the intro cutscene, which is prerendered in 1080p. So that's not going to look all that great in the future (or until like the release of the game, where 4k displays already existed). You don't earn money. You gamble for it. Usual races average around 10.000 credits. The cheapest car costs around 40.000 credits. The most expensive thing you can buy in the game is a house for 5.000.000 credits. The credit reward of every single race combined won't give you enough money to buy that house. Even if you haven't spend anything of it. Even if you didn't upgrade/tune your vehicles. Anytime you level up, you get to play a slot machine. The average reward of a slot machine is around 40.000 credits. The game looks great. I feel indifferent for the car handling. The sound is good. The story is underwhelming. The races are generally fun and the open world also has a charm to it. But, I cannot stress enough, that this game has crashed about 20+ times in my 30 hours of playtime on the newest nVidia driver. There are collision bugs in the stadium as well. There's a drifting mission that has released broken for controller players since it's launch and I am quite certain, that it will not be patched out in this timeline. I was thinking of recommending it, because it is a truly good game. But I just can't recommend a game, that crashes this consistantly. It's like recommending a sportscar, that turns off every time you drive more than 2km. It is nice, but the technical difficulties drag it down in a big way. Either wait for more stable graphic card drivers or hope for a patch. 5/10

I really wanted to like this game, especially after FH 4 which was near perfection for an open world racing game with very few flaws. Sadly after around 8 hours of trying I uninstalled and went back to FH4 as it still is the superior game in my opinion. There are a few areas where this game does improve over 4 but it's not the parts which make the game compelling and give you reason enough to stick around. [u]The Positives[/u] It is graphically superior, performs well outside of a few minor issues and it does fix one glaring problem 4 had which was customisation. FH4 only had 4 engines in upgrades, gearbox choices where limited and aero also had few choices. 5 did improve on this and the engines in 5 sounded a lot better. Driving physics were also tweaked and improved which was a bonus, even if its not driving sim level its a nice touch and adds to the experience. The weather storms are also a neat feature and some of the tracks and scenery is very well detailed and aesthetically pleasing. This however is where the problems begin as the nicer tracks and scenery are very few and far between. [u]The Negatives[/u] Sadly the really fun tracks and beautiful scenery is sparse due to probably the biggest problem this game has, The map itself. It's bigger which isn't the issue, it's what they did with the map which is. In FH4 the map was smaller but the quality was there throughout. It was visually appealing, the seasons were actually distinct and the it had variety be it driving in the north or through small cosy villages. In 5 however due to the location and geography available the huge map just looks very bland, very brown and lacks any charm or distinguishing features for the most part. The lush forests and small town tracks are nice, but due to the lack of enough of it as a whole it just comes across as soulless and uninteresting. It was all too often that the lack of anything interesting on the map meant that instead of seeing places or roads that felt alive and worth exploring it just became tedious. Exploring became dull, races not being helped by uninspired track design and nothing to make them pop visually trackside meant that the fun wasn't there as it was in previous incarnations. When it's pretty it is really well done and the graphics shine but unfortunately there wasn't enough of it. The second glaring issue is the car choice. In FH4 and before there is a good mix of classic cars, current cars, performance cars and a few quirky oddball cars which have a lot of charm going for them. In 5 they really started to swing towards electric cars and made other odd decisions when it came to car choice. Some of the classic cars from previous incarnations are scrapped for a lot of Electric vehicles which visually and sound wise are nowhere near as fun and lack the soul of some of the cars which where dropped for this game. There are a few gems hiding in there and some of the cars available that weren't before are pretty good. The problem is a lot of the newer cars or dlc are either uninteresting, dull to drive or just not on the same level as the ones available on previous games. Pretty much most of the dlc cars in 4 where very good outside of 1 or 2 dlc packs. They all added something new and fitted in nicely with the car roster. In FH 5 however most of the dlc cars are either mid at best or very uninspired. The base roster itself is ok but a lot of the newer additions for 5 just lack the fun element while driving them. The cars you know from 4 are still here but just because they look a bit nicer and sharper doesn't make it worth diving in to this world when the map doesn't justify it anyway. If the new cars where able to add something to the experience it might have been worth staying around, sadly they don't and it's another huge issue that detracts from the game itself. [u]Conclusion[/u] As a product FH5 looks better, has more choice when it comes to customisation and has nice touches which show it could have had potential. Looking at it on paper and in the games detail and performance it is a superior version technically. However it lacks an important aspect: Soul. The map is larger but feels lifeless. The tracks feel like a step backward when it comes to design and very few of the new cars available make it worth hanging around for. FH4 may be technically inferior but for the map, for the racing and for feeling vibrant and alive it is still the superior game. It has charm and a well designed map alongside a very good selection of events and tracks. As it stands 5 is not a terrible product, but lacks key elements that it needs to bring it to life. I couldn't recommend FH5 over FH4.

Forza Horizon 5 feels less like just another racing game and more like an incredible collection of expensive, exclusive cars brought to life in stunning detail. Every vehicle looks phenomenal thanks to the high-quality visuals and resolution—it’s hard not to stop and admire the reflections, paintwork, and environments before hitting the accelerator. What I really enjoy is the freedom to have fun both solo and with friends. Whether I’m cruising across the vibrant Mexican landscapes alone or diving into online events with a crew, the game delivers a smooth, exciting experience every time. There’s a great balance of arcade-style fun and realism, making each race feel rewarding without being overly punishing. Compared to The Crew: Motorsport, Forza Horizon 5 simply feels tighter, more polished, and more enjoyable. The controls are responsive, the variety of cars and customization options are top-tier, and the open world keeps pulling me back in. If you love cars and want a racing game that looks amazing and never gets old with friends, this is the one to beat. ⭐ Rating: 9/10 – Pure driving joy, gorgeous visuals, and endless replay value.

[h1]Bringing The Festival To Mexico![/h1] Your Ultimate Horizon Adventure awaits! Explore the vibrant and ever-evolving open world landscapes of Mexico with limitless, fun driving action in hundreds of the world’s greatest cars. [list] [*][b]220+ Hours on Xbox One[/b] [/list] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ATReviews]Follow My Review Group Here![/url] 💾Graphics - Forza Horizon 5 has really stunning visuals. The vivid colors of the Mexican architecture, the beautiful landscape and dynamic weather makes this game really stand out. Car models also look absolutely incredible! Forza always had amazing visuals! Also the HUD and User interface is really clean and easy to navigate. Everything about this game is perfect when it comes to visuals and graphics. 🎮Gameplay - Forza Horizon 5 has amazing gameplay. It’s honestly where the game shines the most. The amount of variety of cars this game has is incredible, and one of the strongest in the current line up of racing games on Steam. Tons of trucks, electric cars, American muscle, European icons, Japanese legends and tons more! Most cars feel pretty different to some extent, and the tuning options will give you even more freedom to make the cars the way you want them to behave on the road. Being able to share your liveries, and tunes is also a great feature that many players will enjoy. Not to mention the awesome auction house to sell your cars and bid on some rare cars to buy. There are many more amazing features this game has. But what about the racing? Well I’m here to tell you that it’s really good! Many of the AI are fun to race against. I will say that they do feel a bit overpowered in the higher difficulties which can test your skills. The races can range from road races, street races with traffic, drag racing, offroad racing and the challenging cross country races. This form of diverse set of racing makes all of the cars in the game worth using. If you don’t like the race layouts, then make your own! Yes! You can actually design your own races and share them online! There is so much to say, but just know that this is Forza Horizon, you will have many things to do and complete! It’s a blast and hard to find anything wrong with the gameplay. The only thing I didn’t like that much was the map. To me, it’s just the weakest in the franchise. It’s not horrible, but feels kinda lifeless. Not much traffic and the terrain just looks boring at times. Forza Horizon 4 has a better map with challenging roads and dense traffic. Like I said, it’s not a horrible map, just the weakest in the franchise. 🎭Multiplayer - I haven’t played much of the online events, but they are okay for the most part. The battle royale is stupid, but besides that the other events are really fun. The online connection has gotten better since launch, so connecting with your friend and doing races is much easier and not a pain like before. The online mode has something for everyone. Races, infection, hide and seek, and much more! 🕛Playtime - You can sink hundreds of hours into this game. It’s got a lot of races, challenges, track editor, and much more! The replayability is really up to you here. If you love the map and races, or want to create your own races, then you will put in so many hours here. On Xbox alone I have up to 200+ hours. 🎧Sound - Now for the cars, the sound design has seen a massive jump in quality compared to Forza Horizon 4. Many cars sound unique, have a great idle sound to them, and are just much more enjoyable to drive, because of the sound improvements. You can also have anti lag which sounds pretty sick! The music is pretty solid. Probably the weakest in the franchise, but still pretty good in my opinion. I will say the voice dialogue is cringe and gets annoying to hear really fast. Besides that little complaint, the sound design is superb! ❗Bugs❗- I haven’t encountered any bugs in this game. Nothing serious or really anything minor. It was a super smooth experience when it came to bugs. You should have no issues here. 🔅Performance - Performance is incredible! High/Ultra settings and getting 180fps+ on 1600p is just amazing! The game runs flawlessly, no stutters, no crashes. This game is incredibly optimized. ✔️Pro’s✔️ [list] [*]Over 900 cars [*]Incredible visuals [*]Solid soundtrack [*]Great photo mode [*]Upgrading & tuning [*]Amazing optimization [*]Improved handling model [*]Share livery & tunes you created [*]Create your own races and restrictions [*]Tons of fun races and events to complete [*]Much improves car sounds compared to FH4 [*]All Horizon intro's recreated (extra's tab in settings) [*]Many accolades/challenges feel rewarding and fun to complete [/list] ❌Con’s❌ [list] [*]Annoying & cringe dialogue [*]Requires Xbox account to play [*]AI can be unfair on higher difficulties [*]Probably the least interesting map in the franchise [/list] 🏆Rating - 8/10 Buy this game on sale if you want to get the ultimate edition. The game feels like it’s worth full price (standard edition) if you are looking for an open world arcade racing game. 🔗Conclusion - Forza Horizon 5 is a fantastic racing game! I’d describe my experience with Forza Horizon 5 as a love/hate relationship. On the positive side, the game (and the series as a whole) feels like a spiritual successor to classics like Need for Speed: Underground. It offers a wide variety of cars, deep tuning options, and a massive open world to explore, along with a good mix of race types. That freedom and variety are what keep me coming back. That said, I mostly stick to offline play. Online racing has lost a lot of appeal since cheating seems rampant, and just a glance at the leaderboards makes that obvious. Offline racing is decent enough, though the “drivatars” can be hit-or-miss. They usually get the job done, but at higher difficulties their behavior can feel erratic and frustrating. One of my biggest frustrations is car availability. Too many vehicles are locked behind the “Horizon Backstage Pass,” and others are only obtainable through time-limited online events. It feels unnecessarily restrictive, especially for players who do not want to engage heavily with online features. Cosmetics are another mixed bag. Earlier games gave us a nice range of gloves, suits, and hats. This entry instead leans on additions like prosthetics. They may be meant to feel inclusive, but they came at the cost of variety in the more traditional options people actually used and wanted. Another ongoing issue is the unskippable NPC chatter. This problem carried over from previous titles, and unfortunately it is still here. The constant dialogue and forced map interruptions feel more grating than immersive, and I would much rather just get back to driving. In the end, Forza Horizon 5 is still a fun game, but it carries its fair share of irritations. For better or worse, I enjoy it for what it is, though I cannot help wishing it were a little less flawed.

What Works Really Well 1. The Map is Drop-Dead Gorgeous The variety in biomes is incredible: from jungle ruins to coastal beaches to neon-lit cities and towering mountains. The lighting is stunning. The weather systems — especially the dust storms and tropical rain — really make you feel like you're driving through something dynamic. 2. Tons of Cars, and They Feel Great There are hundreds of vehicles, from hypercars to off-road buggies. Whether you're bombing down a highway in a Koenigsegg or drifting through a canyon in a JDM legend, the handling is tight, smooth, and satisfying. You can tweak a lot, but it's also super accessible — anyone can jump in. 3. Smooth Progression Without Pressure Unlike most racers, Forza Horizon 5 doesn’t really punish you for anything. You get rewarded constantly: XP, wheelspins, accolades, cars, credits. It’s less about “winning” and more about enjoying the ride — literally. The game’s tone is relentlessly positive and chill. 4. Online Works Better Than Ever Whether you want to explore solo, co-op races, competitive events, or just mess around in The Eliminator (battle royale mode), Horizon 5’s online is integrated well. Playing with friends is finally smooth, and online events don’t feel tacked on. 5. Accessibility & Customization The level of tuning and control options is insane. Assist settings make it easy for newcomers, while hardcore drivers can go deep with simulation options. There's even a full Event Lab that lets players create custom races and challenges — and it’s surprisingly robust. What Doesn’t Work (Or Got Old) 1. The Festival Vibe Is… Corny The game leans hard into the “car festival” theme. The dialogue is painfully cheerful, the voiceovers can feel scripted to the point of cringe, and everyone acts like you’re some god-tier celebrity driver. It’s meant to be fun, but sometimes it's a little too over-the-top. 2. Repetition Creeps In Yes, there are tons of events… but after 10-20 hours, you start to notice a pattern. Street races blur together. Cross-country events feel similar. If you're not actively switching up how you play (online, tuning, photo challenges, etc.), the core loop can get stale. 3. Bugs & Online Glitches (Especially at Launch) At launch, the game had some rough online connectivity issues. Things are much better now, but every once in a while, you’ll hit a weird bug — like AI cars freezing, races not loading, or leader boards glitching out. Nothing game-breaking, but definitely annoying when it happens. Score: 9/10 “A vibrant, high-octane sandbox that never stops giving — even if it gets a little too friendly sometimes.”

Why the Game is not really worth the price Missed Potential Coupled with Jaw-Dropping Visuals Forza Horizon 5 offers an eye-wateringly beautiful open world packed with a massive car roster and well-realized environments. However, when it should be delivering the genuine car culture experience, especially social car meets and multiplayer sessions, it slips up in many critical areas. Car Meet Experience The game is lacking in good, well-planned car meet spots. Most of the spots are small, uneven, or filled with random traffic that hurts normal meets. The Horizon Cars & Coffee update added a more car meet-friendly spot, but it's small and doesn't address the overall demand for big, adaptive meet spots. Spawn experience desecrates the mood with crass festival tunes and messy settings, clashing with the chill atmosphere car enthusiasts require when gathering. There is no dedicated car meet mode, so there is a makeshift lobby that players must settle for which is often buggy and awkward to manage. Progression and Racing There is a minimalist progression system where players are dropped right into hypercars like Bugattis, spoiling the grind to get through car classes vibe. Tracks are mostly improvised road courses or loops with no real racing curbs, predetermined racing lines, or specific race courses, so racing is lifeless and unsatisfying. Races are shorter and rubber-banded, decreasing challenge and replay value. Car tuning is ancient and restricted, especially compared to modern standards. Multiplayer and Crossplay Crossplay is only available on Xbox consoles and Microsoft Store computers, with Steam players essentially locked out, and social play is impossible. Private meet hosting and car meet hosting are problematic with platform constraints and inconsistent matchmaking, usually capping meet sizes at a handful of players. With a relatively small online community and technical issues, hosting dynamic large-scale car meets is quite a challenge. Final Thoughts Forza Horizon 5 is an incredible idea for a social racing game, but technical limitations and design choices keep it from fostering a lively car enthusiast community. No meet spaces, linear progression, and cringe multiplayer severely restrict the game's allure among players looking for genuine car meet ambiances and meaningful racing experiences. All that aside, the modding community and car enthusiast meet groups try their best to fill in the blanks, but the game itself can do with some actual improvement in these areas. If Playground Games pays attention to these issues in upcoming patches or sequels, then FH5 can truly be a must-have for automotive enthusiasts.

It’s the first racing game that truly hooked me since Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005 — the GOAT). From the moment I launched FH5, I felt like I was 12 again: controller in hand, throwing cars sideways through traffic like a maniac. FH5 doesn’t pretend to be a simulator. It’s big, loud, colorful, unapologetically arcade — and that’s exactly why it works. Cars feel great, the map is gorgeous, and everything flows: races, challenges, stunts, barn finds, dumb little stories… you’re never stuck, and you’re never out of things to do. No need to tune gear ratios or worry about tire wear. Just floor it, drift through a jungle, fly off a cliff, land at 250 km/h into a checkpoint — and the game rewards you with fireworks. Is it realistic? No. Is it fun? Hell yes. That said, it’s clearly designed with consoles in mind. Menus feel clunky with a mouse, you’re constantly interrupted by scripted events and unskippable popups, and the game bombards you with unlocks, pings, and missions you never asked for. Sometimes you just want to drive, but FH5 insists on throwing festival cinematics and new challenges at you. 9/10 — A pure arcade blast that reignites that Most Wanted spark. (But be ready to wrestle the UI if you use keyboard.)

Forza Horizon 5 - A step in the wrong direction. I love Forza. I am a new player, saw a lot of FH3, played 100 hours of 4. I love this franchise, but Forza Horizon 5 sets trends that will kill this franchisw for me. I will compare this game to FH4. ■ The first, worst part of this game is the map design. The map itself is flat, with non-sensical roads without a lot of life in them. There are bearly any landmarks worth remembering, bearly any cities, houses, anything. The map is like the new skate game. The roads were built for racing, not for finding good tracks to race on normal roads. The problem with that is that this game is missing a map that is alive, and even when they made roads purpose built for races, they are not that fun. Sierra Nueva, the map of the rally dlc showed me that playground games is competent when it comes to making good tracks. We will need to see the same quality in FH6. ■ The progression just straight up sucks. I unlocked the final race of the road series in my first play session. FH4 had the progression down to science, and here we got this weird sticker progression that opens up the game way too fast, and honestly. The expedition required to open up each series were boring and irritating to do. I don't mind the game handing me cars left and right, but getting cars is straight up rng. I made more cash in wheel spins, than i did in races. I got better cars by gambling, than by unlocking. The drip feed or cars in playlists makes some online, and completionist features not worth doing. I joined the game right at the end of it's official update cycle. So car pictures are impossible for me to do, since i cannot get playlist exclusive or wheelspin exclusive cars easily. Also the way you get cars amplifies the issue, since you can get like 10 cars in an hour, which makes changing the cars, to take pictures irritating and not worth doing. ■ Online functionality is awful. I don't play with other players because first, there is no rating/penalty system which makes each lobby full of dirty rammers playing bumper cars. Searching for a race is randomized as well since you cannot pick a playlist for the race type/class you want. ■ Drive avatars are a placebo. The A.I doesn't see you, is often confused and the front members are always way too fast. It's just a gimmick to put on a box. ■ Seasons make 0 difference. Weather types make zero difference. Again. Another Placebo, gimmick to put on a box. Horizon 4 changed the way the map worked, and it was fresh and exciting to drive on each season. Now it's just nothing. ■ Most radio stations are grating to listen to. The music doesn't flow, some songs are tied to a track, and some songs hurt my ears. I never got tired of Horizon XS in my 100 hours of FH4, but here i hop stations often. A lot of the time i have the radio turned off. ■ Why did i spend over 100+ hours in this game then? The driving is simply amazing. The feel of the physics is superb, even better than FH4 and the wheel support is good, but not great. They need to improve it further. If they don't fix most of this stuff, i reckon i will not stay with Forza much longer. I have a lot of small things i'm not going to point out, because that would make this a full blown essay. These are the core problems with Horizon right now.

"Forza Horizon 5," developed by Playground Games, is an expansive open-world racing game that takes players to a stunningly realized version of Mexico, blending arcade racing thrills with a deep roster of cars, events, and environments. As the latest entry in the Horizon series, it refines the formula with jaw-dropping visuals, a massive map, and a seamless mix of solo, co-op, and competitive experiences. From dense jungles to dusty deserts, coastal towns to volcanic peaks, Forza Horizon 5 is a visual showcase and a playground of possibilities. The driving is smooth and exhilarating, with hundreds of customizable cars and a seemingly endless supply of races, stunts, and challenges. While some may find the game’s tone overly chipper or its structure familiar, the sheer volume of content and polish makes it one of the best open-world racers to date. Pros: -Gorgeous, massive open world packed with variety and detail. -Huge car roster with deep customization and tuning options. -Seamless online integration and wide range of event types. Cons: -Light narrative and overenthusiastic tone may not appeal to all. -Core structure remains largely unchanged from past entries. Overall, "Forza Horizon 5" is a masterclass in open-world racing, offering spectacle, freedom, and fun in equal measure. It’s the definitive Horizon experience and a must-play for racing fans and casual drivers alike. 9/10

PL Forza Horizon 5 to gra, przez którą prawie zapomniałem, jak się chodzi. Po co wychodzić z domu, skoro mogę pędzić 300 km/h przez Meksyk w Lamborghini, którego nawet nie stać mnie zatankować w prawdziwym życiu? Gra wrzuca cię w sam środek festiwalu, który najwyraźniej nie zna pojęcia budżetu ani ciszy nocnej. Jednego dnia ścigasz się z odrzutowcem, drugiego skaczesz jeepem przez aktywny wulkan. Realizm? Bliski zeru. Frajda? Bliska stu. Mapa jest ogromna, przepiękna i zawsze świeci słońce, kiedy tego potrzebuję. Spędziłem więcej czasu wybierając felgi do auta niż ludzie wybierają mieszkania. Co pokochałem: Przejażdżki przez dżunglę jak w hollywoodzkim filmie akcji Personalizacja aut na poziomie “Hot Wheels na sterydach” Rozwalanie kaktusów i dostawanie za to XP Gra mówi mi, że jestem gwiazdą – częściej niż moja mama Co mnie zabolało: Sztuczna inteligencja czasem jeździ, jakby była jeszcze w trybie uśpienia Sporadyczne bugi (np. auto startuje jak rakieta bez ostrzeżenia) Fakt, że mój prawdziwy samochód nie brzmi jak V12 Podsumowując: Forza Horizon 5 to nie tylko gra – to styl życia. Głośny, błyszczący, bez ograniczeń prędkości i pełen absurdalnych wyzwań. I to jest piękne. 10/10 – ścigałbym się z pociągiem jeszcze raz. GB Forza Horizon 5 is the reason I forgot how to walk. Why go outside when I can race through Mexico at 300 km/h in a Lamborghini I’ll never afford? The game throws you into a festival that apparently has an unlimited budget and no noise complaints. One second you’re drifting down a volcano, the next you’re drag racing a plane. Realistic? No. Fun? Absolutely. The map is massive, beautiful, and somehow always sunny when I need it. I’ve spent more time choosing rims than most people spend choosing apartments. What I loved: Driving through jungles like I’m in an action movie Customizing my car until it looks like a Hot Wheels fever dream Crashing into cacti and getting XP for it Being told I’m a superstar every 10 minutes (I need that kind of energy IRL) What made me cry: The AI sometimes drives like it just woke up from a nap Occasionally gets buggy — like launching me into space buggy The fact that my real car doesn’t make V12 noises In summary: Forza Horizon 5 isn’t just a racing game — it’s a lifestyle. A very loud, flashy, car-filled lifestyle where you’re always the hero and speed limits are optional. 10/10 would race a train again.

Overall Score: 6/10 - The gameplay is engaging and fun, especially with friends. However the problem lies within its half-baked story, bland environment and locked content. Gameplay: 4/5 - The gameplay is quite fun! It feels very intuitive and easy to pick up. Allowing you to play on both controller and wheel. Story: 0/5 - Unfortunately the story feels pretty uninspired, the characters lack much depth and the entire plot doesn't serve much purpose to the game as a whole. Obviously it's not a major part of the game, but it's still apart of it regardless. But easily the worst part about it, is a lack of skipable cutscenes. You have to watch every single one in full, which can get a bit annoying after some time. I'd rather just drive my cars and not be apart of the cutscenes entirely. Difficulty: 2/5 - At first it may be difficult learning how the car reacts to the road, especially if your new to racing games. But fairly quickly you'll get the hang of it without much trouble. Progression: 2/5 - You can get tons of cars for just playing. However some cars are locked behind either DLC, or weekly challenges. Forcing your players into weekly challenges just to unlock certain cars feels pretty bad. Not to mention if there is a specific car you want, you have to pray it comes back, without guarantee it ever will. Replay Value: 3/5 - Single player gets a bit stale. Community: 5/5 - Friendly and not toxic. Graphics: 3/5 - It looks good, but the environment isn't very captivating. Audio: 3/5 - Cars sound nice. The soundtrack isn't particularly astounding. Price: 1/5 - Buy on sale. Conclusion: Do I think FH5 is worth it? That depends on what you want in a racing game. If you want a fun and engaging community with solid gameplay to support it. Then this game is perfect! If you would like to collect every car and be a completionist, then please know it's not really possible in its current state. But that's okay! Because at its core it's a fun game. And that's enough for most people.

Whether you’re a casual player or a hardcore car enthusiast, there’s something here for you. That said, it’s not perfect. The UI can feel bloated, some online features are inconsistent, and while updates keep coming, some bugs and connectivity issues still linger. Also, post-launch content and DLC can feel stretched or overpriced for what you get. Still, if you love cars, beautiful worlds, and pure freedom behind the wheel, FH5 is absolutely worth it. 9/10 – Gorgeous, fast, and fun, with a few speed bumps.

Despite the good level of realism and focus on racing for gameplay, the Forza Horizon series has always been more of a car sandbox than a racing simulator, the races are only there to give a sense of direction and a basis for interacting with other players. While this leads to very fun gameplay, there is a distinct lack of story that comes with the car sandbox genre, Winning races feels meaningless as profit is the only incentive, upgrading vehicles feels pointless as the CPU opponents always scale their vehicles around yours, and I often open the game and have no idea what to do, despite having dozens of unplayed races and undriven cars. Forza Horizon has the same core issue that The Crew did (excluding the first The Crew game, may it rest in peace): there is a massive amount of stuff to do and almost no reason to do any of it. Forza Horizon can be a very fun game, but it's important to know if it's right for you. Horizon focuses on gameplay above all else, even at the expense of story, but the gameplay is enough for a positive review.

Well, it just Forza Horizon 4, but in Mexico. Game is only worth it if it's on sale and NEVER for full price. Played this game a few years ago on the Microsoft store and had an absolutely horrible time with it as it's an arcade and the game doesn't like you using steering wheels. Even had a dev say that this game is for controllers only as it was designed purely for that crowd, unlike Motorsport (any edition) that was designed to be used with a wheel more than a controller. Decided to give this a try after a few years, and watching youtubers play it, and can say that the game is still bad. Not sure how youtubers play the game with a wheel as 900 degree wheel rotation gives you a feeling like you're driving a boat. Reducing the wheel sensitivity helps, but not by much as all the cars act like they have helium in them. Just slightly turning the wheel leaves your car to spin out of control and doesn't act anywhere close to what it's like in real life. Even if you have steering wheel dialed in and have the right tune, the car still flies around corners like it's on helium as brakes aren't a thing in this game. Not sure why brakes don't work in this game, but you have to grind walls in order to slow down cause they didn't feel like making brakes work in the game. And when they do work, they are way too sensitive and will spin you out of control making you have to restart the round so you don't get last place. Car selection is nice, but it's bad when you have 72 cars that can't be unlocked unless you pay additional money to unlock them. I'm not against companies having paid DLC, but then ALL cars should have the option to use real cash in order to acquire cars if someone wants to just spend money on them. And yes, you can buy car voucher packs that will allow you to buy cars in game, but they have too many cars that can only be acquired either during a seasonal event or through backstage pass mode in which case you'd have to grind hard to acquire 1 backstage pass which allows you to buy 1 car and it can't be a car you already own. Too many cars on are the auction house and most players will never own those kinds of cars. Auction house is a complete joke. They restrict people from being able to sell cars beyond a certain price range unless you are tuner/livery creator. And even if you create tunes/liverys, you need a certain number of downloads and likes just to be able to sell a car at a higher value. So if you unlock a car, that you don't like, too bad about selling the car on the auction house as the most you can sell it for is 31k credits. Yeah, no point in using the auction house since you can't sell your cars as you're not a youtuber and there's already tons of tunes/liveries in the game that you won't be able to ever reach the goal of selling cars for 20mil. On top of that, you better have a bottomless wallet as even D rank cars can sell for millions and you most likely will never win the bidding war against the cheaters who go out and buy hacked accounts and acquire cars and money that way. Why is it they were so keen about going after questionable liveries, but are completely fine with people buying hacked accounts and getting all the cars they want and all the money they can get for a few hundred bucks? And whats worse is when youtubers are able to promote hacked accounts, which violate the TOS, and Forza does nothing about it. But you dare have a questionable livery and they ban your account fully. Honeslty, those youtubers need to get account ban for promoting hacks for this game. I pretty much only play it on my Steam Deck and that's cause there's no reason to play it on computer if you need a controller to play the game. Song choices are bad, voice actors are hard to understand, car choices are severly limited unless you pay real cash for cars or buy hacked accounts and transfer cars over that way. The fact that there are tutorials on how to grind money in this game, shows that they can't be bothered by making payouts for races a lot higher than the minimal amount they offer in the game. Such a disappointment and if Microsoft truly gutted the Motorsport division of this company, the next Horizon needs to have elements from Motorsport like the wheel controllers working as intended and fix the turbo. And yes, the turbo is always spooled in the game and it's like they can't be bothered to allow you to hold onto your turbo when going around corners. Those that run turbos in their cars in real life, know exactly what I mean and it just makes the game harder to play because you are instinctly holding RPM's with the idea of keeping your boost at certain levels, only for the game to eithe rgive you full boost, even at lower RPM's. Get it on sale such as the last 50% off sale as it's barely worth the sale. Or if you are exclusively buying it for your Steam Deck so you have more games to play on it.

The first 50 or so hours are enjoyable, however after you collect most of the cars, the game slows down and the grind for backstage passes kills it for me. The passes are an interesting idea, but it just boils down to a "What can we make into a microtransaction in our $60 game?". Don't get me wrong, I think the idea of doing challenges for cars or items is cool, but the grind is too much and after doing it two or three times. The grind only seems to be there not to reward the player, but to incentivize the player to make another purchase. The map, while visually impressive, is too spaced out and not dense enough to make it fun. The roads are too wide and do not convey a sense of speed very well (something Forza 4 was very strong in). The size of the map is great, but I just wish it was more dense, so you really have a lot more to explore. Lastly, the voice acting and writing in the game is one of its largest shortfalls. The writing for the in-game characters is flat and stale. They use this really cheesy spanglish that comes off as tacky and is often annoying. At points it sounds like a children's game, with unnatural speech. This game had the potential to be the best in the series, but unfortunately does not hold a candle to Forza 3 and 4. Especially in the contents that keeps people hooked, which an open-world game like this deserves.

As the 5th installment in the series, and playing all but the 4th title and being a long time Forza Fan, there are somethings they did right and wrong. On the Right (Pros): [list] [*] Beautiful Scenery, its fun to run laps around the map, the mountains and cities in between. [*] There is [b] A LOT [/b] to do and tons of circuits and sprints to do with challenges to do in between. (a pro and con, more on that later) [*] Visually appealing, with changing environments as the seasons pass by. [*] Tons of cars to cruise, test and tune, drift etc. [/list] On the wrong (Cons): [list] [*] Connecting with friends without being able to use the Steam Friends list and being forced to use the Built-in Xbox App on windows is such an awful technical decision, far too cumbersome for something that already works. [*] Lifeless Story that kinda drags on, its not horrible, but it kinda feels like the festival thing has run its course on me. [*] The interactions with the NPCs in conversations are not memorable, i only really recall the "Vocho" Story line, which was alright. [*] The Game OVERWHELMS you with stuff to do (the [strike] engaging [/strike] story lines specifically) , especially if you get into the game late. [*] Starting with high end cars in the garage, its cool i guess, but i really like the build from the low end and build my way up. [*] Copy and Paste exterior mods, specifically the rear wings. There could be more variety, bc some of the performance wings look tacky at best and ugly at worse. [/list] Overall, its a alright game that does well when and where it tries. Highly recommend to play with friends, and pick it up on sale.

This review is coming from someone who played All Forza Horizon games starting from FH 1. [h1]PROS:[/h1] 1- i like it, it's very well optimized, it's really fun and packed with a lot of activities, The graphics are peak, The cars are very diverse and fun, Attention to detail is very well done too. The map is better than FH4's map. 2- Also i am not much of a DLC believer, and i genuinely think most are a waste of money, BUT For FH5's Hotwheels DLC this is a rare exception and a very very fun DLC and well put and very well executed. [h1]CONS:[/h1] 1- The menu UI is although not bad and well got used to by most players since it follows the same design from previous titles. i think it should be worked since it can be a bit overwhelming for new players. and organised a bit more. 2- a other concern is that they need to add an option called something like "Manual+Clutch for Manual-Only Cars" or something along those lines. The reason is that when I drive cars that are auto-only and I fail to clutch and shift properly, I get a gear-up/down delay. I get it for manual cars that makes sense but for auto-only cars, there should be an option that removes that delay, since those cars in real life don't require clutch input in the first place and i hate to switch constantly from Manual+clutch to Manual. or maybe provide the ability to assign a hotkey to quickly switch between the two. It's a small thing, but it would make the experience smoother and more realistic for people who use Manual+Clutch across all cars. but i guess this is just a opinion of mine. In the end i definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes cars. a solid 10/10. Also next fh pls pls pls make it in japan.

So, I caved. I HAD to find out what the hype was about with Forza Horizon 5, and in true impulse-buy fashion, I spent way too much money on it. But to be honest? It was actually pleasantly surprising. The driving mechanics are silky smooth, the cars feel weighty and responsive, and the open-world Mexico setting is stunning. The moment I got behind the wheel and started shredding through sandstorms and street races, I understood why people were obsessed. But here’s the thing no one tells you: driving games eventually start to feel like déjà vu on wheels. No matter how many different cars or race types you try, it slowly becomes the same loop — drive fast, win money, buy car, repeat. Then there’s the auction house. Oh, the sweet, soul-crushing auction house. I spent hours scrolling, watching, waiting… only for that dream car — listed at a decent price — to be instantly snatched up within milliseconds. I’m convinced there’s a secret underground cabal of players using some sort of turbo-click software because by the time my finger touches the button, the car’s gone. Every. Single. Time. That said, I’m no hardcore car fanatic, but even with my casual knowledge, I found the game near-perfect. I'm sure proper car nuts could point out areas that need improvement (tuning, realism, maybe car sounds), but for someone like me? It was just right. In short: If you love cars, racing, or just want to zoom around a digital paradise with vibes and horsepower, Forza Horizon 5 delivers. Just don’t expect the auction house to ever show you mercy.

Stattdessen muss ich ständig weitere DLCs kaufen, um an wichtige Fahrzeuge zu kommen. Das ist eine Frechheit und zeigt, wie sehr die Community vor den Kopf gestoßen wird. Dieses Verhalten schadet der Spielerbindung enorm und wird auf Dauer Forza Horizon in seiner Popularität deutlich schaden. I generally like Forza Horizon 5. The variety of cars and tuning options are impressive and fun. The driving physics are well done, and the game offers many beautiful tracks. However, the game loses its appeal very quickly: after about 20 hours, you basically have everything you need. I bought the Premium Edition with the justified expectation of having access to most of the cars. Instead, I constantly have to buy additional DLCs to get important vehicles. This is outrageous and shows how much the community is being let down. This behavior severely damages player retention and will significantly harm Forza Horizon’s popularity in the long run.

The real issue I have with the game though, and the reason for the overall negative review, is that the entirety of the game's writing/dialogue is atrocious. Bad enough that I mute all of it, turn off all subtitles and sit in silence during the un-skippable cutscenes until I can do the driving bit again. Forza Horizon 5 ★ ★ ★ ★ ★ (5/5 – A Must-Play) Forza Horizon 5 isn’t just a racing game—it’s a celebration of speed, freedom, and automotive culture. Set in a stunning, hyper-detailed version of Mexico, it offers one of the most beautiful and diverse open worlds ever seen in a racing game. From sun-drenched deserts and dense jungles to sprawling cities and active volcanoes, every inch of the map feels alive. And the best part? You can explore it all in hundreds of cars, from classic street legends to modern hypercars, each one feeling distinct and incredibly fun to drive. The gameplay is the perfect blend of arcade fun and realistic handling. Whether you’re drifting through a mountain road, blasting through sandstorms, or launching off cliffs in a 1,000-horsepower monster, it all feels smooth, responsive, and ridiculously satisfying. Horizon Festival events, street races, dirt trails, drag races, stunts, and the wild Seasonal challenges keep things fresh. And with dynamic weather and a full seasonal cycle, no two days feel the same. Add in multiplayer, EventLab custom creations, and regular content updates, and it’s a game you can sink hundreds of hours into. Visually, it's breathtaking. The lighting, detail, and realism are top-tier—especially on PC or Xbox Series X. And the soundtrack? Pure road trip energy. Turn left, hit 200 mph, fly off a volcano. Worth it.

I've not played any of the Forza collection since this game and 2025, but I've wanted to for a long time. I've heard so many good things about the franchise but being a Playstation owner I was never able to play the "XBOX Exclusive" title until now that they've started releasing them on PC. I didn't want to drop a buttload of money on a game that I knew nothing about other than hearing word-of-mouth reviews. I snagged this on the Steam Summer sale and wow! I've been missing out! With the excitement and feel of games like Burnout Paradise, The Crew, and the open world of games such as Just Cause 3 and GTA V...this game is a best of all of those worlds. The car collection is EPIC. There are tons of cars, I already own so many that I've only driven a handful and each time I play they give me 4-5 more! The customization and tuning of the vehicles, while it's a bit daunting, it is worth it. I've been able to turn my older, sluggish cars into tuned monsters. Often times I've found myself just driving for no reason at all, no direction, and finding something to do. Sometimes I start with a goal in mind or a race right at the beginning. Other times it's just about building up skill points and unlocking more goodies. One of the most unexpected things is the rivals within the races. It keeps your friends' track times and car choices and you end up racing against them in races. My older brother passed away Jan 2024 but he was an avid gamer. He owned this game and even though he's gone, I was able to race head-to-head with him drifting around corners and gunning it on the straightaways. The ability to see his gamertag floating above the car next to me was surreal. Looking for a fun arcadey style racer with tons of cars, tons of upgrade options, and a giant open world? You got it right here.

The Good and the Bad of Forza Horizon 5 – Is It the Ultimate Racing Game? Forza Horizon 5 is one of the most visually stunning and expansive racing games ever made—but is it perfect? Let’s break it down: The Good 👍 ✅ Stunning Graphics & World Design – Mexico’s open world is breathtaking, with dynamic weather, dense jungles, and gorgeous deserts. ✅ Huge Car Collection – Over 500+ cars, from classic muscle cars to hypercars, all with incredible detail. ✅ Smooth Gameplay & Physics – Whether you're a sim racer or an arcade fan, the driving feels responsive and fun. ✅ Endless Content – Races, challenges, story missions, and seasonal events keep the game fresh for months. ✅ Great Soundtrack & Atmosphere – The radio stations and festival vibe make cruising around a joy. The Bad 👎 ❌ AI Still Feels Unfair (Sometimes) – The "Drivatars" can feel rubberband-y, especially on higher difficulties. ❌ Online Issues at Launch – Server problems and connectivity bugs were frustrating (though mostly fixed now). ❌ Repetitive After a While – If you’re not into collecting cars or doing similar events, it can get grindy. ❌ Microtransactions Exist – While not pay-to-win, some car packs and cosmetics are locked behind extra payments. Verdict? Forza Horizon 5 is one of the best open-world racing games ever, offering insane visuals, tons of cars, and endless fun—but it’s not without flaws. If you love racing games, this is a must-play. What’s your take? Love it or overrated? Drop your thoughts below!
